title: Recommend entries carry execution_alias_retention (openrouter spec §2.3, D15)
description:
openrouter spec §2.3: each POST /v1/recommend recommendations[] entry carries "execution_alias_retention": {alias: effective retention mode} beside execution_aliases. 5.4 emits execution_aliases but not execution_alias_retention, so maverick-core's recommend client (which decodes it) sees every alias as unknown, and the proxy's OpenRouter mode (6.10) would skip every alias for a zero-retention tenant.

# Fix
Emit execution_alias_retention right after execution_aliases in entry_json, using maverick_api::models::alias_retention (5.5: each execution_aliases key with its effective mode; missing or expired evidence reads as unknown). Update the declared golden test's Rust-field insertion, and assert the field in the execution-aliases test (including an expired alias).

# Done when
Tests pass. Commit.
close_reason: Completed: recommend entries carry execution_alias_retention (D15)

title: OWNER: judge_rubric spend is outside the G8 cap and is not recorded; confirm before the first live nightly
description:
What main does, verified 2026-09-29:
- The spend guard (spec 11, G8) projects only runs: sum over task x column x repeats of est_in x p_in + max_tokens x p_out. Its actuals are sum(runs.cost). So neither side counts the judge_rubric grading calls.
- Each judge-graded run makes 2 judge calls (order swap; batch.rs test judge_disagreement_feeds_ambiguity: 3 gradings, 6 calls) on the judge pool (seed gemini-3.1-pro and gpt-5.5, both premium). High-stakes tasks may use panels.
- maverick/src/serve.rs ProviderJudge::complete keeps only response.text and drops the usage. Judge tokens and cost are recorded nowhere: not in runs, not in the batch output, and not in a metric.

This matches the spec as written (the G8 formula counts runs) and so is not a bug. But it affects two owner steps:
- 9.6: the first live nightly 'under the spend cap' has uncapped judge spend on top. On cold-start nights every judge-graded task runs on every column x 3 repeats.
- 9.8: the retune 'from M6 cost measurement' will understate the provider bill by the judge calls.

Options:
(a) Measure only (recommended first step, no G8 change): record judge input/output tokens and cost per batch, for example on the batch completion record and log and as a metric, so M6 and 9.8 see the full bill. The 9.15 spend preview could also report the count of judge-graded runs.
(b) Also cap: add an estimated judge cost to the projection and the recorded judge cost to the actuals. This changes G8 behavior, so it needs a spec change and a DIVERGENCES row.
(c) Accept as is, and size the provider-side budget with judge calls in mind.

Filed by SnowyHorizon while fixing model-maverick-8mfe (the resume double count in the same guard).

title: Fix batches claim race: concurrent first claims raise 23505 on batches_pkey
description:
crates/maverick-store/tests/batches.rs concurrent_claimers_leave_exactly_one_lease_holder fails in about 2 of 3 runs on main (75b6679). claim_batch returns: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "batches_pkey" (23505), Key (id)=(bat_nightly_2026-09-28) already exists.

Cause: crates/maverick-store/src/batches.rs inserts with 'on conflict (kind, batch_window) do nothing'. That names one arbiter index. The id is deterministic from (kind, batch_window), so a concurrent insert of the same row can hit the primary key first, and Postgres raises the PK violation instead of doing nothing.

Fix direction: 'on conflict do nothing' with no arbiter (both unique constraints describe the same row), or treat 23505 as the lost race and fall through to the existing-lease path. Then rerun the test in a loop (for example 20 times) to show it is stable. Found while gating model-maverick-rust-port-3hk.4.7.
close_reason: Fixed: claim_batch insert uses 'on conflict do nothing' with no arbiter, so a concurrent first claim that collides on batches_pkey (deterministic id) is absorbed and falls through to the FOR UPDATE path. Reproduced before the fix: 3/10 runs of concurrent_claimers_leave_exactly_one_lease_holder failed with 23505 on batches_pkey; after: 0/20 runs of the full batches suite failed. .sqlx entry for the changed query replaced.

title: Clean up the permanently failed graphile row left by a duplicate enqueue followed by a worker crash
description: graphile_worker's add_jobs, on a key whose job is locked (running), clears that job's key and sets its attempts = max_attempts, then inserts a new job with the key (migration m000019). If the worker running the original then dies, the recovery sweep unlocks it, but it can never run again: it stays in _private_jobs as a permanently failed job. The duplicate job rescues the window (serial queue, then a lease takeover resumes the batch), so no work is lost, but spec 11.2 acceptance says no permanently failed jobs are left behind. Found while writing 7.12 (crates/maverick-jobs/tests/crash_restart.rs). Options: delete such rows in the batch tail transaction (same task identifier and window, attempts >= max_attempts, unlocked), or avoid re-enqueueing a locked key. Add a crash_restart scenario: enqueue while running, then kill -9, then restart; assert the queue ends empty.
close_reason: Fixed: batch completion transaction deletes the m000019 permanently-failed orphan (key null, attempts exhausted, unlocked) via maverick-store batches::delete_orphaned_failed_jobs. Deterministic crash_restart test reproduces the orphan and proves the completion removes it (negative control fails without the fix); full crash_restart suite green (9/9), clippy clean. Spec 11.2.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Analysis (DustyForest, 7.14). Option A: switch JobKind::job_spec to JobKeyMode::UnsafeDedupe. add_job then only bumps the revision of an existing keyed job, locked or not: no duplicate, and the running job's attempts stay intact. Cost: a permanently failed job keeps its key, so an operator's re-enqueue of that window would be silently ignored (preserve_run_at resets attempts and revives it). Option B (preferred): keep preserve_run_at; in each leased job's completion transaction, delete unlocked rows of the same task identifier whose key is null and attempts >= max_attempts and whose payload window equals this window (parse the payload with JobArgs::window). The serial default queue means the duplicate only runs after the original released the queue, so the original is either deleted (success) or unlocked and exhausted by then. Test: crash_restart scenario 'enqueue while running, then kill -9, restart' asserting an empty queue.

title: CI: cargo deny fails on main since 2026-10-12 (rustls 0.23.45 has 4 advisories, yoke-derive 0.8.3 is yanked); bump the lockfile
description:
Every CI run on main since ee529b7 (2026-10-12) fails in the fast tier at the deny step. Push runs, the nightly schedule, and the a7d0 ubuntu-26.04 canary all fail the same way, so the runner image is not the cause.

# Findings (nightly run 39218291797, 2026-10-19)
- yanked: yoke-derive 0.8.3. Fix: cargo update -p yoke-derive.
- RUSTSEC-2026-0346, -0347, -0348, -0349 on rustls 0.23.45. Each is fixed in rustls >= 0.23.46.
  - 0346: derived Debug on client session values prints TLS secrets. It affects only a custom ClientSessionStore that formats them. The crates have none.
  - 0347: buffered data goes to the outer server after ECH rejection. It affects only EchMode::Enable. The crates do not use it.
  - 0348: Brotli certificate decompression can allocate 1 GiB. It needs the brotli feature, which is off (rustls in Cargo.lock has no brotli dependency).
  - 0349: an unauthenticated ServerHello can fix a later key share to classical X25519. This one can apply: the provider clients use reqwest with rustls and resumption on. The impact is loss of post-quantum confidentiality only.

# Side effect
In scripts/ci.sh, run_fast runs deny before the sqlx offline check, parity_coverage --strict, and the instrumentation lint. So those three gates have not run on main since 2026-10-12. The fix must show all three green.

# Work
1. In a clean copy of HEAD, run cargo update -p rustls -p yoke-derive. The diff must touch only Cargo.lock and only those crates (plus any lock lines they pull in). Do not take the shared tree's Cargo.lock, because it carries lines for peers' uncommitted manifests.
2. cargo deny check with the CI flags must pass.
3. Verify fmt, clippy, and the tests. Local builds are refused by rch while it has 0 workers. Get the owner's call on how to verify before you commit.
4. Push. The push run's fast tier must be green end to end.

# Done when
A main push run has a green fast tier, with deny, sqlx, parity-coverage, and instrument all run.
close_reason: 4a59a39; push run 39325795947 green end to end

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text: Done. 4a59a39 changes only Cargo.lock: rustls 0.23.45 to 0.23.46 and yoke-derive 0.8.3 to 0.8.4, two versions and two checksums. The tempfile getrandom edge that cargo update wanted to move stays at 0.4.3. The owner chose to let CI verify, because rch had 0 workers. Push run 39325795947 is green: fast ran engine-boundary, fmt, clippy, test, deny (advisories ok), sqlx, parity-coverage (836/836), and instrument, and db, e2e, parity, and changed-line mutants all passed. It is the first green main run since 2026-10-12. ckgy is unblocked.

title: Redact credentials in MAVERICK_SMTP_URL from Config Debug output (G5)
description:
# What
`maverick-config`'s `impl Debug for Config` prints `smtp_url` verbatim (crates/maverick-config/src/lib.rs, the `.field("smtp_url", &self.smtp_url)` line). The URL format is `smtp://[user:pass@]host[:port]/?from=..&to=..` (reference Part 3 §4.3), so it can carry the SMTP password. `alerts_webhook_secret` is already redacted; the SMTP password is not.

# Why
G5 / spec §14.3: credentials never appear in a log line or span. Any `tracing::debug!(?config)` or panic message with the config would leak it.

# Fix
Print the URL with the userinfo password replaced (for example `smtp://user:<redacted>@host:587/?from=..&to=..`), or print only `<set>`/`<unset>`. Add a unit test that the Debug string of a config with `smtp://u:hunter2@h/?from=a@x&to=b@x` does not contain `hunter2`.

Found by CrimsonCarp while wiring alert delivery (bead 3hk.7.11).
close_reason: Fixed: Config Debug now redacts every URL that can carry a credential: database_url, smtp_url, and otel_exporter_endpoint go through redact_credentials (userinfo password and any password= query value -> <redacted>), and alerts_webhook_url prints its origin only (Slack/Discord-style webhooks keep the secret in the path). Test plants a canary in each URL, the internal token, the webhook secret, and a provider key: none appears in format!("{config:?}").

title: CI: cargo deny fails on every main run since 2026-10-12 (yanked yoke-derive 0.8.3; rustls 0.23.45 advisories RUSTSEC-2026-0346 to 0349)
description:
The fast tier fails at cargo deny on every main run since 2026-10-12. The latest is run 39218291797 (schedule, 18772e8, 2026-10-19). fmt, clippy, and test pass before it. The sqlx check, parity coverage, and instrumentation lint run after deny, so they have not run on main since then.

# Findings
- error[yanked]: yoke-derive 0.8.3 (first seen 2026-10-12).
- error[vulnerability]: rustls 0.23.45 has RUSTSEC-2026-0346, 0347, 0348, and 0349 (first seen 2026-10-19). 0.23.46 fixes all four.
- Exposure: 0349 (an unauthenticated ServerHello downgrades later connections to classical key exchange) applies in principle to every reqwest client and to the alerts SMTP client, because rustls keeps resumption on by default. 0346 needs a custom ClientSessionStore, 0347 needs EchMode::Enable, and 0348 needs the brotli feature. Cargo also moves the tempfile edge from getrandom 0.4.3 to 0.3.4 (MSRV-aware re-resolution). That edge change is not needed: with it kept at 0.4.3, cargo metadata --locked passes. The final diff is 2 packages (version and checksum each).
- Verified locally: cargo deny check --hide-inclusion-graph -A duplicate -A license-not-encountered prints "advisories ok, bans ok, licenses ok, sources ok".
- Not verified locally: build, clippy, and tests. rch refuses them on this host (0 workers).

title: Write the root README and the docs/architecture/ set
description:
The repo has no root README.md. Write one, plus full architecture documents under docs/architecture/.

## README.md (repo root)
Follow README good practice. Sections, in this order:
1. Name and a short statement of what Model Maverick is: a B2B recommendation engine for LLMs. It benchmarks models nightly against a private corpus, classifies workloads, applies tenant policy, and returns a ranked fallback chain. The engine does not execute inference; only the trial proxy does, with the caller's credentials.
2. Status badge for the GitHub Actions CI workflow.
3. Key ideas / guarantees in plain language (summarize G1 to G14 from specs/model-maverick-v1-spec.md; link to it, do not copy it).
4. Architecture overview: one Mermaid diagram (GitHub renders it) of the main components (API, core, domain, store/Postgres, jobs via graphile_worker, runner, providers, proxy, alerts, sdk-conformance) and how a request and the nightly benchmark flow through them. Link to docs/architecture/ for detail.
5. Repository layout: a table of every crate in crates/ with a one-line purpose, plus specs/, parity/, reference/, plans/, docs/, scripts/.
6. Getting started: prerequisites (Rust toolchain from rust-toolchain.toml, Docker for testcontainers, Postgres, cargo-deny, cargo-mutants, sqlx-cli at the versions CI pins), clone, build, configure (env vars and config; list each with its purpose and default), run the database migrations, run the engine and the proxy locally, and make a first request.
7. Testing: scripts/ci.sh and each tier (fast, db, parity, e2e, mutants, mutants-diff), SQLX_OFFLINE and scripts/sqlx-prepare.sh, the deterministic fake provider, and that CI never calls real providers.
8. Contributing: point to AGENTS.md, the beads workflow (br / bv), and the git rules (work on main, stage by name).
9. Links to docs/api.md, docs/onboarding.md, docs/operations.md, and the specs.
10. License section (ask the owner if the license is not decided; do not invent one).

## docs/architecture/
Write one index (docs/architecture/README.md) plus one document per area. Suggested set: overview and component map; request path (recommend: classification, policy, pools, ranking, fallback chain); nightly benchmark pipeline (corpus, runner, pacer, scoring, EWMA/Welford, regressions, spend cap G8); data model and store (Postgres tables, migrations, sqlx offline); jobs and scheduling (graphile_worker kinds, cron, leases, SIGTERM rule); trial proxy (hosted and self-hosted modes, chain execution, credentials); telemetry and outcomes (/v1/telemetry, no POST /v1/outcomes); privacy and zero retention (G1, G5, D1, debug capture encryption); observability (tracing, skip_all rule, OTLP); testing and parity strategy (parity/, DIVERGENCES.md, mutation testing). Use Mermaid for flows and sequence diagrams.

## Rules
- Describe the Rust code as it exists in crates/. Verify each command by running it. Mark any part that is not built yet as planned, and link its bead id.
- Follow the AGENTS.md writing rules: short specific sentences, no em or en dashes mid-sentence, none of the banned words.
- Never include corpus content (task prompts, golden answers, rubrics), real keys, or the deploy host details.
- Link to specs/ as the authority. Do not restate normative contract text in a way that could drift from it.

## Done when
README.md and docs/architecture/ exist, every setup step was run on a clean checkout and works, all links resolve, Mermaid diagrams render on GitHub, and the work is committed and pushed to main.
close_reason: Root README.md (all 10 sections, Mermaid architecture diagram, crate table, getting-started, CI tiers) and docs/architecture/ set (index + 10 area docs: overview, request-path, trial-proxy, nightly-benchmark, data-model, jobs-and-scheduling, telemetry-and-outcomes, privacy-and-zero-retention, observability, testing-and-parity). Written to AGENTS.md style rules.

title: Proxy OTel emission (D31): maverick.recommendation log record, recommendations counter, W3C trace context, redaction canary
description:
Split out of model-maverick-rust-port-3hk.6.9 (which keeps telemetry wiring D27 and rate limiting D28).

# What
Reference Part 6 §12 and §18 (T-otel-*); spec v1 §8.1 and §14.3; D31, D19.
- Enabled iff MAVERICK_PROXY_OTLP_ENDPOINT is non-empty; disabled means no exporter task and no connection (T-otel-disabled: the collector receives 0 requests in 250 ms).
- Export through opentelemetry-otlp (HTTP) with service name MAVERICK_PROXY_OTLP_SERVICE_NAME (default maverick-proxy). Follow crates/maverick/src/otel.rs (5.14). The logs signal needs the 'logs' features of opentelemetry-otlp and opentelemetry_sdk in the root Cargo.toml.
- One log record per settled request (relay or exhaustion; never 400 or engine_error): body maverick.recommendation, attributes recommendation_id, surface (chat_completions | messages), mode, model_used ('' on exhaustion), attempts, final_status (502 on exhaustion), measured (bool), classification_method.
- Cumulative monotonic counter maverick_proxy_recommendations_total with attributes measured as the STRING 'true'/'false' (QUIRK 18) and classification_method.
- Payload bytes are not reproduced (D31); tests decode the OTLP payload and assert content. T-otel-happy, T-otel-cold (fixtures otel_happy_path_log_record, otel_measured_false_fallback_counted), T-otel-cumulative, T-otel-disabled; tag D31.
- W3C trace context propagated to the engine and to the provider call; D19 redaction canary (no prompt, body, or credential in any exported attribute).
- Fail-open; flush on shutdown with a bounded timeout.

# Seam
maverick_proxy::surface::ReportSink gets one ChainReport per settled request after the relay ends. 6.9 adds the fields OTel needs (mode, model_used, final_status) and the ProxyReports sink; add the OTel recorder beside Telemetry there.

# Done when
Tests pass. Commit.
close_reason: Proxy OTel (D31): ProxyOtel records one maverick.recommendation log record per settled request (relay or exhaustion) with the section 12.1 attributes and increments maverick_proxy_recommendations_total (measured as string, classification_method), exported over OTLP/HTTP (SDK batch log processor every 5 s, cumulative counter every 15 s) only when MAVERICK_PROXY_OTLP_ENDPOINT is set; fail-open; bounded flush at shutdown. W3C: global TraceContext propagator; the caller's traceparent/tracestate now reach the engine (RecommendClient::recommend_traced); providers already get them. Tests decode the real OTLP protobuf from a mock collector against the fixture templates: T-otel-happy, T-otel-cold, T-otel-cumulative, T-otel-disabled, a D19 canary test, and trace context to the engine. No new packages (two lock edges for test decoding).

title: Provider model discovery: detect new models from connected providers, plus a manual refresh endpoint
description:
Owner decision 2026-09-30: the engine learns about new models from the connected providers' own model-list APIs, never from models.dev or another third-party feed. The operator can also trigger a refresh by hand through an internal endpoint, and enroll new models from that call. Enrolled models start the normal cold-start window.

Why: today nothing notices a model release. New columns come only from a manual `POST /internal/v1/columns`, so the catalog and the judge pool fall behind (for example, Sonnet 5.5 shipped 2026-09-30 and the defaults still name gemini-3.1-pro, gpt-5.5, grok-4, claude-sonnet-4-6). `price_sync` reads models.dev only for prices of hand-mapped columns and ignores every other model in the feed.

Scope:
1. Adopt the decision (next free D number, D51 unless taken) into the spec, DIVERGENCES.md, docs/api.md, docs/operations.md.
2. A model-list call in each hand-written provider client, plus the fake provider.
3. Discovery: compare provider lists to the catalog, a daily job, and alerts.
4. `POST /internal/v1/models/refresh`: run discovery now, and optionally enroll models as cold_start columns.

Out of scope: auto-enrolling models without an operator call (enrollment spends money under the G8 cap), prices from provider APIs (they return none), re-pointing the judge pool (spec §6.4 keeps that empirical and manual).

Timing note: a new column is `cold_start` for `catalog.cold_start_nights` (default 5) and its cells become `measured` after `scoring.min_nights` (default 3) nights. The "three-day" period the owner described is the measured threshold.

title: Adopt provider model discovery (D51) into the spec, DIVERGENCES.md, and docs
description:
Write the provider model discovery decision into the documents before code lands (AGENTS.md: owner approval, then a DIVERGENCES.md row and a spec update).

Work:
1. Take the next free D number (D51 unless taken; D47 looks unused, check) and add a DIVERGENCES.md row: new behavior with no Go counterpart.
2. Spec (`specs/model-maverick-v1-spec.md`): the discovery job in the jobs catalog (name `model_discovery`, cron, env override), the new alert kinds and severities in the alert catalog, the new internal endpoint in the endpoint and error catalogs, and the config keys.
3. `docs/api.md`: `POST /internal/v1/models/refresh` request, response, and every error code.
4. `docs/operations.md`: a "New models" section: how discovery works, how to enroll, spend impact, and that judge re-pointing stays manual (§6.4).
5. `plans/master-plan.md` decision list.

Design points to fix in the spec (propose, then ask the owner if unsure):
- Sources: only providers with a configured operator key (`MAVERICK_*_API_KEY`). A provider without a key is skipped and reported, never an error.
- Filter: text chat models only. Drop embeddings, audio, image, moderation, and fine-tune ids. Decide per provider how dated snapshots and moving aliases (for example `-latest`) are treated; prefer the pinned snapshot id.
- Output sets: `new` (listed by the provider, no catalog column with that provider and model_id), `withdrawn` (a non-retired catalog column whose model the provider no longer lists).
- Alerts: `new_model_available` (info, one per model, deduped until enrolled or dismissed) and `model_withdrawn` (warning).
- Privacy: model ids are not sensitive, but no request bodies or keys in logs (G5).
close_reason: D51 is in the spec (§4.6, §11, §13, §14.1), DIVERGENCES.md, docs/api.md, docs/operations.md, and the master plan; the alert kinds and their D51 test are in maverick-alerts.

title: POST /internal/v1/models/refresh: run discovery on demand and enroll models as cold_start columns
description:
`POST /internal/v1/models/refresh`: the operator's manual trigger for provider model discovery, with optional enrollment.

Behavior:
1. With an empty body, it runs discovery now (the same code as the `model_discovery` job, synchronously, with a timeout) and returns `new`, `withdrawn`, and per-provider status (`ok`, `skipped_no_key`, `failed`). It writes the same alerts as the job.

4. Enrollment is all-or-nothing in one transaction.

Errors (each has a contract test, AGENTS.md): `401` bad internal auth; `422 invalid_request` for a bad body, a missing price, or an entry that is not in the `new` set; `409` when a column already exists; `503` when every provider failed. Use the existing error catalog codes where they fit.

Auth: internal API only (operator). Tenants never trigger discovery or enrollment, because enrollment spends operator money.

title: Resumed batch double-counts its done runs in the spend guard: a crash, deploy, or timeout mid-batch can refuse the resume and skip grading and the rebuild
description:
run_batch projects the FULL batch on every delivery (project(&groups, repeats) ignores the done triples), then check_spend adds the night/week actuals, which already include the earlier attempt's runs. So a resumed delivery counts each done run twice: its actual cost in night_spent plus its projected cost.

Go had no resume (D10: each retry minted a new batch_id and re-ran everything), so there the full projection was the true forward cost. D10 made Rust resume from existing runs, so the guard must project only the remaining (task, column, repeat) triples.

Failure: caps sized near the projection (what 9.15 enables), attempt 1 allowed at 80% of the nightly cap spends 50% and dies (Kamal deploy SIGTERM, kill -9, the 6 h batch timeout on a cold-start night). Attempt 2 sees 80% + 50% = 130%: Refuse, lease finished Skipped before grading. The spent runs are never graded or folded, no aggregate_rebuild, and a spurious critical spend_refusal fires. This breaks plan 3.1's acceptance (kill -9 / restart / handler timeout each end with exactly one completed batch, one rebuild, and the correct alerts). crash_restart and batch tests use default caps with fake costs, so they never cross a cap.

Fix (maverick-jobs batch.rs): read the done triples before the guard; guard projection = sum over (task, column) of (repeats - done count) x per-run cost; keep the full projection for planned_runs / completion_pct; when nothing remains, skip the guard and grade + complete. A first delivery is unchanged (done is empty), so Go parity fixtures are unaffected.

Test: real Postgres, seed attempt-1 runs under the lease's batch id with known costs, take over, run_batch; with caps where full+actual > cap >= remaining+actual, the batch must complete, rebuild, and raise no spend_refusal. Negative control: without the fix it is refused.
close_reason: Fixed: a resumed batch's spend guard projects only its remaining runs (each task, column pair's repeats less its done runs). A first delivery is unchanged; with no runs left the guard is skipped and the batch grades, completes, and rebuilds. Tests (tests/batch.rs, hand-computed): resumed_batch_projects_only_its_remaining_runs (9/15 done, $0.045 spent, $0.10 cap: before $0.117585 refused, now $0.074043 runs) and resumed_batch_with_no_runs_left_skips_the_guard; both fail on the old code. On HEAD 80e183c: batch 14/14, crash_restart 9/9 (handler_timeout hit its 90 s SETTLE once at load 100 in the parallel suite and passed alone in 32 s), clippy -D warnings, fmt. Also validated rebased onto TealHarbor's uncommitted 9.15 batch.rs.

title: D2: the zero-retention classifier accepts evidence from a sibling column, not the column it calls
description:
# The gap (found in a zero-retention audit, 2026-09-30)
Spec §8.3: the zero-retention classifier call uses classifier.zero_retention_column, "a column whose effective retention_mode is zero". If "its evidence has expired", the prompt-form request is refused (422) and the prompt never leaves the engine.

crates/maverick-api/src/classify.rs does not check that exact column:
- The classifier is built from find_column: the FIRST catalog column (ordered by id) whose model_id and endpoint match the model/endpoint ref. The call uses that column's provider client.
- The request-time D2 check, has_zero_evidence, accepts the ref when ANY catalog column with that model_id and endpoint has valid zero evidence.

So with two columns of the same model and endpoint, a zero-retention tenant's prompt goes to the first column's provider, while the evidence can come from the sibling. The sibling can differ in settings (thinking on/off), or in provider, because the ref names no provider. This fails open under contradictory catalog data, in a rule that must fail closed. The spec needs no change: it says "its evidence".

# Fix
has_zero_evidence checks only the column find_column picks (the called column), with the same effective-retention rule as D1 (recommend::effective_retention).

# Test
The D2 suite (crates/maverick-api/tests/classify.rs, real Postgres):
- the first column by id is standard, and a same-model sibling (other settings) has valid zero evidence: refused, no call, no cache row;
- the reverse: classified on the zero-retention classifier.

# Noted, not in scope
§8.3 also says the zero-retention classifier column is "covered by the G4 simulations like any pool member". No simulation or downgrade alert references it today, so a downgrade gives 422s with no operator alert. Checked separately.
close_reason: has_zero_evidence checks only the column find_column picks (the called column); new D2 test fails on the old any-column rule. classify, classify_redaction, classify_reconnect, debug, recommend_prompt green.

title: OWNER: let the internal column API read back retention evidence and param_constraints (reply keys or a GET)
description:
# Question for the owner

What main does (verified 2026-09-30, crates/maverick-api/src/internal.rs column_json):
- POST /internal/v1/columns and PUT /internal/v1/columns/{id} reply with Go's column shape: column_id, provider, model_id, endpoint, settings, execution_aliases, status, pricing, quality_source_column_id, cold_start_until, deprecation_date, created_at, updated_at.
- They accept and store the retention evidence (retention_mode, retention_verified_at, retention_valid_until, retention_source; D1, D15), execution_alias_retention, and param_constraints (D29). The reply echoes none of them.
- The internal API has no GET for a column. The only read of those fields is the tenant-authenticated GET /v1/models, which shows the effective retention_mode (expired evidence reads as unknown).

Why it matters at go-live: runbook section 5 writes the retention evidence for every launch column, but tenant #1 exists only from section 7. So the operator cannot read back the stored evidence while setting up the catalog. A wrong mode (for example standard instead of zero) is not a safety risk, because zero retention fails closed: a zero-retention tenant gets 409 no_compliant_columns. But it only shows up when a tenant hits it.

The reply shape is pinned by recorded Go exchanges (parity/blackbox/api-recorded.jsonl, and tests/internal.rs asserts the key order). So any change is a new intended difference and needs a DIVERGENCES row.

# Options
(a) Echo the stored fields in the create and update replies, after the Go keys: retention_mode, retention_verified_at, retention_valid_until, retention_source, execution_alias_retention, param_constraints. It needs a D-row. The recorded exchanges then match on the Go keys, with the added keys explained.
(b) Add GET /internal/v1/columns and GET /internal/v1/columns/{id} (root; the full stored record, including the raw and effective retention_mode). New routes, which Go answered 404, so it needs a D-row. The create and update replies stay Go's.
(c) Accept as is. The runbook adds a step: create tenant #1 first, then check GET /v1/models with its key.

Recommendation: (b). It keeps Go's reply bytes. It gives the operator and the Rails shell one root read for audits, and later for the D44 cache prices. After a yes, the runbook section 5 gains a check step.

title: G5/D19: the classifier-failure log line can carry the classifier's completion and provider error bodies
description:
classify.rs logs 'classifier failed; answering the fallback classification' with error = %ClassifyError. Its cause is the last attempt's error text:
- a parse error such as: capability "<model text>" is not a v1 capability. That is the classifier's completion, and a classifier that echoes the prompt puts prompt text in a log line;
- a provider error, whose text includes the provider's raw JSON error body (POST <url>: <status> <reason> <body>).

G5 and D19: prompt text, completions, request bodies, and credentials never appear in spans, log fields, or metric labels. The canary test cannot see this, because its fake classifier never echoes the prompt.

# Fix
Log a redacted summary: the column, the calls, and the cause class. A provider error gives its provider, kind, status, and attempts, without the body. A parse error names the failed check without the model's value. Deadline and timeout stay as they are. ClassifyError's Display stays Go's (parity: TestClassifyErrorNamesColumn).

# Done when
A test with a classifier that echoes a canary into capability, and one whose provider error body carries a canary, shows neither canary in any captured log line. The api suites stay green.
close_reason: The classifier-failure warn line logs ClassifyError::redacted(): the column plus the failed check (parse errors) or provider/kind/status/attempts (provider errors), never the model's text or the provider's body. ClassifyError's Display is unchanged (parity TestClassifyErrorNamesColumn). tests/classify_redaction.rs (3 tests, init_test_tracing_with_secrets): an echoing classifier, a provider error body, and a malformed answer; all three fail on the old log line with the canary in it, and pass now. Green: classify 18, classify_reconnect 1, recommend_prompt 15, debug 39, mcp 11, metrics 1, contract 7, replay 5; clippy -D warnings; fmt; instrument lint; parity_coverage --strict.

title: Cut the declared recommend path's cost (~16-19 ms API CPU and ~10 DB round trips per request) so p95 < 50 ms holds
description:
# Finding (bead 9.3 harness, scripts/latency.sh, release binaries)
On the shared dev host the declared POST /v1/recommend misses the M6 target (p95 < 50 ms). The harness splits engine cost from host noise:
- API CPU per request (from /proc/<pid>/stat): /up 1.4-2.0 ms; GET /v1/models 5.9-8.4 ms; declared recommend 12.9-18.8 ms.
- Database transactions per declared recommend (pg_stat_database): 9.9-11.7.
- Same run's floor: Postgres select 1 p50 1.6-3.2 ms; insert+commit p50 2.5-4.8 ms; /up p50 3-4 ms.
- Declared, 1 client: p50 48-80 ms, p95 114-236 ms (host load average 15-30 on 16 cores).
So roughly 1 ms of API CPU per database query plus a few ms of ranking; that is far above what sqlx and the domain code should cost, and it is what the proxy's added TTFB mostly is (its engine call).

# Work
1. Profile the declared path (a CPU profile of `maverick serve --api-only` under `scripts/latency.sh`; perf needs perf_event_paranoid <= 2, or use an in-process sampler / tracing timings).
2. Likely suspects to check: per-query pool acquire with sqlx's default test_before_acquire ping; one acquire per query instead of one connection per request; statement cache misses across a 16-connection pool; the request/auth middleware's own queries (api key + tenant) on every call; logging/tracing overhead; JSON trace building.
3. Cut the round trips where the spec allows (for example read pools, weights, and constraints in one query), keeping every response byte and the trace row unchanged (the API replay 5.15 and the history/recommend tests must stay green).

# Done when
scripts/latency.sh shows the declared API CPU per request and DB transactions per request clearly lower, and MAVERICK_LATENCY_ASSERT=1 passes on a quiet host. Record before/after numbers in the close reason.
close_reason: Declared path 10 -> 6 DB transactions per request (exact); API CPU 16.25/12.80 -> 15.15/7.60 ms, /v1/models CPU 6.90/7.65 -> 5.10/3.65 ms, 1-client p50 104/104 -> 94/46 ms (alternating base/new A/B on a host at load 49-67). Pool pings only after 30 s idle; auth in 1 query; tenant context in 1 query concurrent with the catalog; availability concurrent with cells. The quiet-host MAVERICK_LATENCY_ASSERT=1 run is model-maverick-j3tt (needs the deploy host).

title: Conversation affinity: keep a conversation on one column unless a switch is worth it (D44)
description:
# Goal

Keep a multi-turn conversation on one model column unless a switch is worth it, so the provider prompt cache is not thrown away for a marginal gain. Proposed divergence D44. The full design is `plans/conversation-affinity-plan.md`. Read it first.

# Why

The proxy and SDK cores call `/v1/recommend` on every turn and nothing ties a conversation to a column. The pick can move between turns (the projection changes the classification, the nightly aggregates change, two columns are close). A move from, say, Opus 5.5 to Fable 5.1 on turn 10 pays full input price plus the cache-write premium for the whole history, and time to first token goes up. The ranking cannot see this: benchmark cost ignores cache tokens and pricing has no cache prices. Example in plan §1: $0.04 vs $0.09 on benchmark cost, $0.10 vs $1.59 for the real turn.

# Owner rule (2026-09-30)

The default is the best model for the turn. Cost does not decide the pick unless the caller asks. Cost-aware affinity (turn cost plus incumbent bonus) is opt-in: `tenant_constraints.affinity_cost_aware`, default false, with a per-request `affinity.cost_aware` override. With it off, the ranking is exactly today's; the engine only reports `kept` or `switched` (`best_model`).

# Shape

- `POST /v1/recommend` accepts optional `affinity {key, context_tokens?}`.
- The engine stores the last pick per conversation in Postgres (`conversation_affinity`, key HMAC'd per tenant, TTL 24 h).
- With cost-aware on, ranking (spec §7.4) adds the turn's context cost (cache-read price for the warm pinned column, cache-write or input price for the others) and a 1.5-point incumbent bonus, withheld on difficulty escalation. Pool, allowlist, standing constraints, zero retention, preference partition, and availability floor all still win.
- Response `affinity {status: new|kept|switched|broken, previous_column_id, reason, cache_warm}`.
- Telemetry moves the row to the column that actually served the turn.
- Proxy: `X-Maverick-Conversation` header in, stripped upstream, `X-Maverick-Affinity` header out. SDK core: `conversation_id` option plus conformance vectors.
- A request without `affinity` is byte-for-byte unchanged (Go parity).

# Done when

Every child bead is closed, the spec and `parity/DIVERGENCES.md` carry D44, and the end-to-end multi-turn test passes.

title: OWNER: confirm the conversation affinity open questions (plan §9)
description:
OWNER: confirm the open questions in `plans/conversation-affinity-plan.md` §9 before D44 goes into the spec.

The owner asked for conversation affinity on 2026-09-30 and approved it as a divergence in principle. These points need a yes or a change. Each has a recommendation, and the other beads assume the recommendation.

1. Defaults: incumbent bonus 1.5 quality points; warm-cache window 300 s; TTL 24 h. Recommended: accept, retune from M6.
2. Derived key in the proxy when no `X-Maverick-Conversation` header is sent. Recommended: not now; later as opt-in.
3. `context_tokens = ceil(body bytes / 4)` overcounts base64 images. Recommended: accept for v1.
4. Telemetry moves the affinity row to the served chain entry. Recommended: yes.
5. DECIDED 2026-09-30 by the owner: cost-aware affinity is a tenant setting `affinity_cost_aware`, default off, with a per-request override. Default is always the best model for the turn. No per-tenant bonus value.
7. Cost in the default ranking: `balanced` (the default mode) weighs cost at 0.35 and all modes break near-ties toward the cheaper column. Make `quality` the default mode, or let a tenant set its default mode? Recommended: decide separately from D44; callers can send `mode: "quality"` today.
6. SDK core in-memory per-conversation pick during an engine outage. Recommended: not in this change.

Done when: the owner's answers are recorded in this bead and in plan §9 (edit the plan if an answer differs from the recommendation), then close it.

comments.author: ubuntu
comments.text:
Plan review (SilentOwl, 2026-09-30). I checked the plan against main at c4e8bf4. It raises no new owner question. Four points should go into the spec text (gcd2.2) or the beads before the build:

1. MCP breaks the Go byte parity (§5.3 against §11). tools/list is Go's list byte for byte (mcp::TOOLS_LIST). It is recorded in parity/fixtures/api/mcp.json and replayed by crates/maverick-api/tests/replay.rs. If recommend_model's input schema gains `affinity`, that exchange no longer matches. So the D44 row must also name "MCP tools/list: recommend_model gains affinity" (and spec §12), and the replay needs an explained exception. §11 says the replay passes unchanged, which it cannot while §5.3 stands. The other choice is to leave MCP out of D44 v1.

2. The HMAC key on the declared path (§4.2, §4.11). affinity_hash needs tenants.prompt_hmac_key. Since e3x (c4e8bf4), the declared path reads no tenants row. Auth reads the key and the tenant's status (get_key_auth_by_hash), and get_tenant_context reads pools, weights, constraints, and the corpus version. Only the prompt path calls get_tenant. Suggestion: return prompt_hmac_key from get_key_auth_by_hash, and compute the hash before the context read. Then fold the affinity row read into get_tenant_context's single query. The declared path then stays at 6 DB transactions, not 7 or 8. The key must stay out of Debug output and logs.

3. "Same transaction as the recommendations insert" (§4.6). Today the trace write (decisions::create_recommendation) is one statement, with no transaction. BEGIN, INSERT, UPSERT, and COMMIT would add 3 round trips to every affinity turn. A single statement with a data-modifying CTE is atomic in one round trip: `with r as (insert into recommendations ... returning id) insert into conversation_affinity ... on conflict (tenant_id, affinity_hash) do update ...`.

4. The telemetry follow rule and OpenRouter (§4.7, D15). In hosted OpenRouter mode the proxy reports model_used as the entry's execution_aliases.openrouter slug and endpoint_used as "openrouter" (crates/maverick-proxy/src/surface.rs). Telemetry items carry no chain index. So "match a chain entry by model and endpoint" never matches there. The rule does nothing for OpenRouter callers, and index 0 is not recognized as index 0. Suggestion: an entry matches when (model_used, endpoint_used) is its (model, endpoint), or when endpoint_used names one of its execution_aliases keys and model_used is that alias's value. Also, the row's primary key is (tenant_id, affinity_hash), so "update where the row's recommendation_id is R" scans every row the tenant has. Either index (tenant_id, recommendation_id), or read affinity_hash from R's trace block and update by primary key with `and recommendation_id = R`.

title: Add the conversation_affinity table, affinity hash, and store functions (D44)

title: Ranking affinity: best-model default, opt-in cache-aware cost and incumbent bonus (D44)
description:
Implement the affinity adjustment in the ranking (D44, plan `plans/conversation-affinity-plan.md` §4.3 and §4.4). Pure domain code in `crates/maverick-domain` (`ranking.rs` or a new `affinity.rs`), no SQL.

Inputs: the survivors after §7.1 and §7.3 with their `Q`, `C`, `L`, `A`, `clears_difficulty`, pricing; the exclusion list; an optional affinity context `{pinned_column_id, cache_warm: bool, context_tokens: Option<u64>}`; config `incumbent_bonus`.

Rules (plan §4.3). The affinity context carries `cost_aware: bool`. When it is false, the order is exactly the no-affinity order (no turn cost, no bonus); only the status is computed, and a moved pick is `switched` with reason `best_model`. When it is true:
1. Turn cost: when `context_tokens` is present and every survivor has `input_per_mtok`, `C'_i = C_i + n * r_i / 1e6`; `r_P` = P's cache read price when warm and present, else each column's cache write price when present, else its input price. `C'` replaces `C` only in `nC` and the noise-band cheaper-first tie rule. If any survivor lacks an input price, skip the turn cost for all.
2. Incumbent bonus `b` added to `Q_P` for the band test, `nQ`, and the noise-band test. Displayed score stays real `Q_P`.
3. Withhold the bonus when P has `clears_difficulty: false` and another survivor has `true`.
4. Preference partition (§7.4 step 5) and availability floor (step 6) unchanged.
5. Status and reason per plan §4.4: `new`, `kept`, `switched` (`escalation`, `outranked`, `preference`, `low_availability`), `broken` (the exclusion reason of P). Reason strings are a closed serde enum.
6. Return the numbers the trace needs: `C'` per survivor, bonus applied or withheld and why.

Parity: with no affinity context the function returns exactly today's order for every existing ranking fixture in `parity/`. Remember the FMA note in memory: use `f64::mul_add` wherever the existing ranking does, and do not change existing arithmetic.

Tests (golden values calculated by hand in the test data): cost-aware off equals the no-affinity order for every existing fixture and reports `kept` / `switched`+`best_model`; kept within the bonus; switched beyond it; turn cost flips a close cost-mode ranking (use plan §1 numbers); cold cache charges P the write price; escalation withholds the bonus; preference violator and low-availability P lose; missing price skips turn cost; bonus 0 still applies turn cost; each `broken` reason. `cargo-mutants` on the new code passes (bounded loops, round-trip tests).

Done when: tests and mutants pass, committed and pushed.

title: Wire affinity into POST /v1/recommend, the trace, metrics, and MCP recommend_model (D44)

Work:
1. Request (`crates/maverick-api/src/recommend/request.rs`): optional `affinity {key, context_tokens?}` with strict decoding. `key` 1 to 256 chars; `context_tokens` integer 0 to 10,000,000; `cost_aware` optional boolean. Errors `422 invalid_request` with `details.field` `affinity.key` / `affinity.context_tokens` / `affinity.cost_aware`; unknown field inside `affinity` is `422 invalid_request`.
2. Config: `affinity.enabled`, `affinity.ttl`, `affinity.cache_warm_seconds`, `affinity.incumbent_bonus` with the `MAVERICK_AFFINITY_*` env names and defaults from plan §4.10, validated at startup.
2b. Constraints: `affinity_cost_aware` in the constraints payload of `PUT /v1/config/constraints` and `PUT /internal/v1/tenants/{id}/constraints` (and the GET that echoes constraints), default false. The effective value = request `affinity.cost_aware` if present, else the tenant setting.

4. Response: `affinity {status, previous_column_id, reason, cache_warm, cost_aware}` after `telemetry` and before `classification_quota_exceeded`; absent when the request had no `affinity`. Pick entry `reason` text per plan §4.5.

6. Metric `maverick_affinity_decisions_total{status, cost_aware}`. No key, hash, or column in labels, spans, or logs; every new `#[instrument]` uses `skip_all`.
7. MCP `recommend_model` input schema gains the same `affinity` object (update `TOOLS_LIST` and its snapshot).

Tests: tenant default off (ranking identical to a no-affinity request); setting on through the constraints endpoint; request override both ways; a contract test per error; key order with and without `classification_quota_exceeded`; each status end to end against real Postgres; zero-retention tenant whose pinned column loses evidence gets `broken` with `standing_constraint:zero_retention`; request without `affinity` byte-identical to today (replay harness green); extend the §14.3 canary test with a canary in `affinity.key`; declared-path latency check with and without affinity stays inside p95 50 ms on the local benchmark harness.

description:

title: Bind maverick-testdb Postgres containers to 127.0.0.1 only (currently public on 0.0.0.0)
description:
SECURITY. crates/maverick-testdb/src/server.rs:72 starts postgres:16-alpine via testcontainers GenericImage without a host IP, so Docker publishes the port on 0.0.0.0 (seen live: 0.0.0.0:33216->5432, user/password maverick). This host has no /etc/docker/daemon.json and an empty DOCKER-USER chain, and Docker-published ports bypass ufw. So while tests run, a Postgres superuser with a known password is reachable from the internet at the host's public IP. A superuser can run shell commands in the container (COPY ... PROGRAM).

Fix in code (do not change the host firewall or Docker daemon config; the owner handles the host side):
1. Make every testcontainers container in the workspace publish only on 127.0.0.1. Options: a host-config modifier that sets PortBindings HostIp=127.0.0.1, or an explicit mapped port bound to loopback. Check the testcontainers crate version in Cargo.lock for the right API.
2. Grep the workspace for any other container or listener that binds 0.0.0.0 in tests, and fix those too.
3. Consider a random password per container instead of the fixed 'maverick'.
4. Add a test that starts the test server and asserts, via the Docker API (docker inspect PortBindings), that HostIp is 127.0.0.1.

Done when: running the db tier shows the containers bound to 127.0.0.1 only ('docker ps' Ports column), the new test passes, and the work is committed and pushed to main.

title: OWNER: do the no-prompt/no-completion log rules (G5, spec 14.3) cover benchmark runs (corpus text, judge replies, benchmarked outputs)?
description:
Spec §14.3 (a G5 control, D19) says prompt text, completions, request bodies, and credentials never appear in spans, log fields, or metric labels. It has no tenant qualifier. G7 says the corpus never leaves the engine through a public API. It says nothing about operator logs.

# What the benchmark path logs today (crates/maverick-jobs/src/batch.rs:494, WARN 'grading: grader failed', error field)
- judge_rubric provider failures: 'judge_rubric: judge <ref> call n/2: <provider error>'. A provider error ends with the provider's raw JSON error body. The judge request carries the corpus task prompt, the rubric, and the benchmarked model's output.
- judge reply parse errors: 'parsing judge reply: json: unknown field "<key>"'. The key is judge model output.
- grader spec errors (key_facts, golden_answer, json_schema): these quote corpus spec content.
The runs table stores benchmark outputs and provider error text (runs.output, runs.error) by design (Go parity). This question is only about log lines.

# Options
(a) §14.3 covers benchmark runs too. Redact these log fields the way bxvh did for the classifier (a489fdb): provider, kind, and status only; the failed check without quoted text. It needs no D-row, because D19 already says no completion in logs.
(b) §14.3 covers tenant traffic only. Operator logs may carry corpus and benchmark text. Add one line to spec §14.3 saying so.
(c) Split: redact provider error bodies and judge replies (model output), and keep the corpus spec errors, which an operator needs to fix a task file.

Recommendation: (c). A corpus author needs the spec error text to fix a task. Model and provider text in logs has no operator use that runs.error does not already give.

Found by CrimsonCarp during the G5 audit (bxvh). SilentOwl agreed it is an owner call (rz6z thread).

title: Production proxy and OpenRouter-style model names (D45, D46)
description:
# Goal

Make the proxy (`maverick-proxy`) a production path, remove the old try-it label (the word matched by `tr[i]al`) from the whole repository, and move model names to OpenRouter's grammar. Proposed divergences D45 (model names) and D46 (proxy fail-open). Full design: `plans/production-proxy-plan.md`. Read it first.

# Owner decisions (2026-09-30)

- No try-it label anywhere. A caller tries Maverick by changing the base URL and changes it back if they do not like it.
- The proxy is production: it follows G14 fail-open like the SDK cores.
- Model names follow OpenRouter's own form (`<author>/<slug>[:variant]`, router `openrouter/auto[:variant]`): `maverick/auto`, `maverick/auto:balanced`, `maverick/auto:cost`, `maverick/<pool>[:variant]`; a non-`maverick/` string is a direct model call with no routing. Settings opt-out is the header `X-Maverick-Settings: caller`.
- `maverick/auto` means the best model (`quality` mode).
- Engine down: last good list, then a configured default model, then `503 engine_unavailable`; zero-retention rules hold.

- The engine knows no billing, plan, or free-period state. That is control-plane business logic. The engine knows tenant status and numeric limits only.

# Done when

Every child bead is closed, the spec and `parity/DIVERGENCES.md` carry D45 and D46, `scripts/ci.sh` fails on any `tr[i]al` match outside `.beads/` and the control-plane spec, and on billing terms in engine source, and the acceptance tests pass.

5. `X-Maverick-Fallback: last_known_good|default_model` on fallback responses. Telemetry for a last-good response uses the cached recommendation id; default-model responses send none.

title: Port the Model Maverick engine to Rust (engine, proxy, conformance harness)
description:
# Goal

Build the Model Maverick engine in Rust so that it gives the same results as the earlier Go engine, except for the approved differences in `parity/DIVERGENCES.md` (D1 to D39 as of 2026-09-28; the owner adds rows, agents never do). The engine includes the proxy (`crates/maverick-proxy`) and the SDK conformance harness (`crates/sdk-conformance`). Source: `HANDOFF.md`, `plans/master-plan.md` §7.0.

# What the product is (background for every child bead)

Model Maverick (MM) is a B2B recommendation engine for LLMs. It benchmarks model "columns" (provider, model, endpoint, settings) every night against a private task corpus (10 capabilities x 5 difficulty tiers), classifies each incoming workload, applies tenant policy, and returns a ranked list of models (the pick plus a fallback chain). The engine never executes inference for customers. The only MM component that executes inference is the proxy, and it uses only the caller's credentials. Four layers: MEASUREMENT (catalog, corpus, runner, graders, scoring, aggregates, calibration), DECISION (classification, policy engine, ranking), ACCOUNTABILITY (prompt hash, decision trace, debug capture, alerts), PLATFORM (tenants + keys, Postgres jobs, the internal seam, MCP, proxy).

# Why this is a port with a complete reference

An earlier Go engine implemented most of v1. Its exact behavior and all 675 of its tests were extracted on 2026-09-28 into:
- `reference/engine-reference.md` (about 4,300 lines, Parts 1 to 7: store/config/CLI, measurement-io, measurement-core, decision, API/MCP, proxy, SQL catalog). Search it; do not read it end to end.
- `parity/` : `fixtures/<area>/` (inputs plus full-precision expected outputs), `manifest/<area>.json` (every Go test mapped to its replacement), `schema/` (migrations, `schema.sql`, 98 sqlc queries), `blackbox/` (619 recorded HTTP exchanges plus 1,498 seed SQL statements), `DIVERGENCES.md`.
The Go source is NOT available and is not needed. Never try to find, run, or rebuild it. Where specs name Go tools (chi, pgx, sqlc, goose, River, `cmd/`, `internal/`), use the Rust stack.

# Owner decisions already made (2026-09-28)
Fresh database; corpus in the private repo `donnfelker/model-maverick-corpus`; hosted plus binary proxy; direct execution by default (OpenRouter opt-in); classifier limits 1000/tenant/day and $5/day (placeholders); models.dev price source; M6b commercial gate suspended (the project may be open-sourced); divergences D26 to D39. Remaining owner items are end-of-project only: provider keys and the deploy host.

# Order of authority when documents disagree
1. `specs/` (the engine contract is `specs/model-maverick-v1-spec.md`)
2. `parity/DIVERGENCES.md`
3. `reference/engine-reference.md` (exact strings, constants, order, quirks)
4. `plans/master-plan.md`

# Work packages (children of this epic) and their order
1. Workspace + CI gates. Blocks everything.
2a. Pure domain crates. 2b. Schema, store, config, CLI. 2c. Provider clients, fake provider, runner. (2a, 2b, 2c run in parallel.)
2d. HTTP API, MCP, internal seam (needs 2a + 2b); proxy + maverick-core (needs 2a; replay needs a mock engine).
2e. Jobs on graphile_worker (needs 2a, 2b, 2c).
3. SDK conformance harness (needs maverick-core and the proxy).
4. Port completion: manifest audit, privacy/canary tests, latency checks, deploy, go-live, first live nightly (owner-gated).

# Definition of done for the whole port (HANDOFF §5)
- Every entry in `parity/manifest/*.json` has a passing Rust test, or an approved row in `DIVERGENCES.md`.
- The API replay (`parity/blackbox/`) and the proxy replay (`parity/fixtures/proxy/scenarios.json`) have zero unexplained diffs.
- CI gates pass: `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy -- -D warnings`, `cargo test`, `cargo deny`, `cargo-mutants` on the domain crates.
- The first live nightly on Rust completes below the spend cap (needs the owner). The owner chose a fresh database (2026-09-28), so there are no Go-vs-Rust distribution checks. The Go implementation was never shipped.

# Rules that apply to every child (from AGENTS.md, guarantees G1 to G14)
- A package is complete only when its Rust tests pass the parity data for its area. Compiling is not enough. No package is done with a diff that is neither fixed nor matched to a DIVERGENCES row. A `QUIRK:` in the reference is Go behavior to reproduce unless DIVERGENCES lists it.
- Do not add a new intended difference yourself. Ask the owner; after approval add a DIVERGENCES row and update the spec.
- Privacy (G5): never store a prompt except in an encrypted debug-capture window; no prompt, completion, request body, or credential in spans, logs, or metric labels; every `#[tracing::instrument]` uses `skip_all` plus an allowlist.
- Zero retention fails closed and outranks G1 and G14.
- Corpus is private (G7): never copy task prompts, golden answers, or rubrics into this repo.
- No real provider calls in CI; use the deterministic fake provider. One opt-in, spend-capped live smoke test only.
- Spend is capped (G8). Pools are hard boundaries (G2). No schema translation. No `POST /v1/outcomes`. No Redis. No MM-owned provider keys for customer traffic.
- Git: plain git, stage by name, one commit per unit of work with the co-author trailer, no push or PR without owner approval.
- Do not compare live benchmark runs for equality (5.37% of model-question pairs flip across identical runs).

title: Package 1: Cargo workspace, crate layout, and CI gates
description:
# Goal
Create the Cargo workspace at the repo root with crates under `crates/`, and make every CI gate from AGENTS.md run and pass on an empty build. This package blocks every other package. Parity gate: CI is green on an empty build (HANDOFF §4 row 1, master plan §6).

# Why first
Every later package needs: a crate to put code in, the shared parity-fixture test helpers, the Postgres testcontainers helper, and CI gates that fail loudly. Setting the gates before code exists stops lint debt from growing (clippy `-D warnings`, the bare-`#[instrument]` lint, `cargo deny` license/advisory policy).

# Required crates (AGENTS.md, plan §4 and §6)
- `maverick-core` : the Rust copy of the shared SDK core (recommend client, chain executor, fail-open ladder, telemetry batcher, alias grammar, workload projection). The proxy depends on it by path.
- `maverick-proxy` : the trial proxy binary (no database, own deployment).
- `sdk-conformance` : mock engine plus mock provider, twelve frozen scenarios.
The agent decides how to divide the engine crates. Guidance: keep pure domain logic (no I/O, no SQL) in crates that `cargo-mutants` can run on quickly; keep the store (sqlx) in its own crate; keep the API (axum) free of business logic (spec §2.2 rule: API has no business logic; recommend and policy contain no SQL; everything reaches Postgres through the store). A split workspace also manages compile times (plan §11 risk).

# Stack (AGENTS.md)
Rust stable, 2024 edition. Tokio, axum + tower, sqlx 0.9 (compile-time checked, offline mode in CI), `graphile_worker` 0.13.x, reqwest + rustls (no OpenSSL anywhere), hand-written provider clients, `jsonschema` (draft 2020-12), serde + a maintained serde YAML crate, `rmcp`, `tracing` JSON + `tracing-opentelemetry` + `opentelemetry-otlp`, RustCrypto (`hmac`, `sha2`, `hkdf`, `aes-gcm`, `subtle`), `ulid`, testcontainers, `insta`.

# Children
Workspace skeleton; CI gate pipeline; instrument lint; parity fixture test-support crate; manifest coverage checker; Postgres testcontainers helper.

# Required crate names (AGENTS.md)

# Suggested engine split (the agent decides; record the final layout in a short `crates/README.md`)
- `maverick-domain` (or several small crates): ids, task/grader types, graders, scoring, EWMA, ranking, policy, ceilings, bands, checks, reasons, predictions math, spend math, catalog lifecycle, capture crypto, fingerprints, key format, classifier pure logic, telemetry derivation. Pure: no tokio I/O, no sqlx. This is what `cargo-mutants` runs on, so keep it fast to build.
- `maverick-store`: sqlx pool, migrations, queries, transactions.
- `maverick-config`: env parsing and validation.
- `maverick-providers`: provider clients, fake provider, retry.
- `maverick-runner`, `maverick-jobs`, `maverick-api` (axum + MCP), `maverick-alerts`.
- `maverick` (bin): CLI entry, wiring (`serve`, `migrate`, `corpus`, `mcp-stdio`, `demo-run`).
- `parity-support` (dev-only): fixture loading helpers (separate bead).
Dependency direction: api -> services -> domain; store is the only crate with SQL; domain depends on nothing I/O-bound.

# Stack pins
tokio, axum, tower, tower-http, sqlx 0.9 (postgres, runtime-tokio, tls-rustls, macros, migrate), graphile_worker 0.13.x (pin exact minor; plan says own a fork if it stalls), reqwest (rustls-tls, no default features), jsonschema, serde, serde_json, a maintained serde YAML crate (not the archived serde_yaml), rmcp, tracing, tracing-subscriber (json), tracing-opentelemetry, opentelemetry-otlp, hmac, sha2, hkdf, aes-gcm, subtle, ulid, rand (CSPRNG via OsRng), testcontainers, insta, proptest.

# Also
- `.gitignore` for `target/`.
- No OpenSSL in the dependency tree (cargo deny will enforce).
- Workspace compiles with `cargo build --workspace` and `cargo test --workspace` (zero tests OK).

# Done when
`cargo build --workspace`, `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` pass. Commit.

title: Set up CI gates: fmt, clippy -D warnings, test, cargo deny, cargo-mutants, sqlx offline
description:
# What
A CI pipeline (GitHub Actions workflow file plus a local `scripts/ci.sh` or `just`/`make` target that runs the same steps, so agents can run CI locally without pushing) with these gates, from AGENTS.md "Tests and quality gates":
1. `cargo fmt --all --check`
2. `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
3. `cargo test --workspace` (Postgres tests via testcontainers need Docker in CI)
4. `cargo deny check` with a `deny.toml`: license allowlist, advisories, bans (ban `openssl`, `openssl-sys`, `native-tls`), sources (crates.io only unless a pinned git fork of graphile_worker is needed). The owner may open-source the project (2026-09-28): allow only permissive licenses (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD-2/3-Clause, ISC, Zlib, Unicode-3.0, MPL-2.0 as file-level) and deny copyleft (GPL, AGPL, LGPL) so any later open-source license choice stays possible.
5. `cargo mutants` on the domain crates only (slow; a separate job, and run locally before committing a domain unit per plan §6).
6. sqlx offline mode: `SQLX_OFFLINE=true` in CI with the `.sqlx/` query cache committed; `cargo sqlx prepare --check --workspace` fails if the cache is stale.
7. The bare-`#[instrument]` lint (bead 1.3).

# Test tiers (the script grows as later beads land)
Structure the script and workflow as named tiers so later beads only register their suite: `fast` (fmt, clippy, unit tests, no Docker), `db` (testcontainers store and job tests), `parity` (manifest coverage checker from bead 1.5 in report mode, later strict; API replay 5.15; proxy replay 6.11; conformance 8.3), `e2e` (full-stack script 9.10; job crash acceptance 7.12), `mutants`. `scripts/ci.sh <tier>` runs one tier; no argument runs all but `mutants`. Every tier writes logs and test reports to `target/ci/<tier>/` and the workflow uploads that directory as an artifact on failure, so a red run can be diagnosed without re-running.

# Rules
- No real provider keys in CI, ever. No network calls to providers. The live smoke test is `#[ignore]` and env-gated.
- The private corpus is never available in CI; corpus tests skip when `MAVERICK_CORPUS_DIR` is unset.
- Do not push or open PRs without owner approval; the workflow file is committed locally.

# Done when
The local CI script runs every tier (empty tiers pass) and is green on the empty workspace. Commit.
close_reason: Completed

title: Add a CI lint that rejects bare #[instrument] (G5 telemetry redaction control)
description:
# What
A CI check that fails if any `#[tracing::instrument]` / `#[instrument]` attribute lacks `skip_all`. Every instrument must use `skip_all` with an explicit allowlist of `fields(...)`. A bare `#[instrument]` records every argument via Debug, which could put a prompt, completion, request body, or credential into a span.

# Why (D19, plan §6, spec §14.3)
Telemetry redaction is a G5 control. Prompt text, completions, request bodies, and credential headers (`Authorization`, `x-api-key`, `X-Maverick-API-Key`) are never span attributes, log fields, or metric labels; fingerprints only. The Go engine used slog JSON logs; the Rust engine adds OTel, so this lint is new.

# How
A small script (grep/ripgrep or a tiny Rust xtask using `syn`) over `crates/**/*.rs`. Prefer the syn-based xtask so multi-line attributes are handled. Include a self-test: a fixture file with a bare instrument must fail the check.

# Done when
The lint runs in the CI script, fails on a bare instrument, passes on the workspace. Commit.
close_reason: Completed: crates/instrument-lint (token-based checker: bare, missing skip_all, ret/err, cfg_attr, macro bodies, renamed import) plus scripts/check-instrumentation.sh with a bad-fixture self-test; wired into scripts/ci.sh fast

title: Build the parity-support test crate (fixture loading, float compare, DIVERGENCES helpers)
description:
# What
A dev-only crate used by every package's tests to read `parity/` data consistently.

# Features
- Locate the repo root and load `parity/fixtures/<area>/<file>.json` with anchor support: manifest `where` values look like `fixtures/decision/policy_evaluate.json#section/case-id`. Provide `fixture(area, file)` and `case(anchor)` helpers returning `serde_json::Value` or a typed struct.
- Float helpers: exact f64 compare; compare-at-tolerance (the reference gives 1e-12 for map-order summation); and `as_f32_widened(x)` for values that Postgres stores as `real` (float32) and Go widened to float64. Many expected values (quality bars, pass rates, EWMAs) are float32-widened; the reference marks each one.
- A `divergence!("D6")` marker macro or attribute-style comment convention that a test uses when it asserts the Rust expected column instead of the recorded Go value, so the manifest checker can see it.
- Loading of `parity/fixtures/measurement-io/testdata/**` and `parity/fixtures/api/testdata/**` raw files (YAML tasks, schemas, prompt text) byte for byte.

# Notes
- Data and contracts in parity (SQL, prompts, schemas, error strings, headers, wire bytes) were copied byte for byte. Never normalize whitespace when loading prompt text or wire bytes.
- Remove the stray `.DS_Store` files only if the owner agrees; they are harmless, ignore them in loaders.

# Done when
Helpers exist with their own unit tests and are used by at least one smoke test that loads a fixture from each area. Commit.
close_reason: Completed

title: Build the manifest coverage checker (every Go test has a Rust test or a DIVERGENCES row)
description:
# What
A tool (xtask or test) that reads `parity/manifest/*.json` (api 256 rows, decision 105, measurement-core 173, measurement-io 144, proxy 66, store 92; 675 Go tests total, 640 unique names, subtests listed separately) and reports, for each `go_test` entry, the Rust test that replaces it or the `DIVERGENCES.md` row (D1 to D39 today; read the file, do not hard-code the list) that explains why not. It fails when an entry has neither.

# Why
AGENTS.md parity rule: "Each Go test in `parity/manifest/*.json` must have a Rust test that replaces it, or a DIVERGENCES.md row that explains why not." HANDOFF §5 makes this the first item of the definition of done. Without a mechanical check, coverage drifts silently (plan §11 "port drift" risk).

# Suggested mechanism
A mapping convention the checker can read, for example a doc comment or attribute on each Rust test: `/// parity: decision/policy.TestEvaluatePoolRestriction` (use the exact `go_test` string), or a checked-in `parity/rust-map.toml` generated and maintained per package. The checker greps the workspace for the tags and joins against the manifests. Report per area: covered, divergence-justified, missing. Also flag Rust tags that name a Go test not in any manifest (typos).

# Rollout
Run it in CI in report mode at first (packages are incomplete), and make each package's closing bead require zero missing entries for its area. The final completion bead turns it to strict mode.

# Done when
The checker runs locally, prints per-area coverage, and has a strict flag. Commit.
close_reason: Built parity-coverage manifest checker (bin in parity-support): parses parity/manifest/*.json, scans crates for 'parity:' tags, matches DIVERGENCES rows; per-area report + --strict; 13 tests; detects 12 existing tags and D37 on real data

title: Build the Postgres testcontainers helper for store and job tests
description:
# What
A shared test helper that starts Postgres 16 (image `postgres:16-alpine`, matching the Go suite) with testcontainers, runs the engine migrations, and hands out isolated databases per test (create database from a migrated template for speed, or a schema per test). Support an env override (for example `MAVERICK_TEST_DATABASE_URL`) to use an existing server, mirroring how the Go recording used `API_TEST_DATABASE_URL` when Docker was unavailable.

# Why
AGENTS.md: store tests and job tests use real Postgres (testcontainers), never mocks. The API replay also needs one real database. Float32 `real` storage, `timestamptz` behavior, and transaction semantics only match on real Postgres.

# Notes
- Migration runner comes from package 2b; until it exists, the helper can accept a migration closure. Wire the real migrations when 2b lands.
- Keep container startup to once per test binary (a `OnceCell` / `LazyLock`).
- The job acceptance tests need to kill and restart workers against the same database; expose the connection URL, not only a pool.

# Done when
A sample test creates a database, runs a trivial query, and tears down; works with Docker and with the env override. Commit.
close_reason: Completed: crates/maverick-testdb. One postgres:16-alpine container per test binary (Go storetest parity: db/user/password maverick, ready line x2, 2 min timeout), Schema (empty/sql/sqlx migrator/custom, chainable) applied once to a hashed template db, one cloned db per test, dropped on close/Drop. MAVERICK_TEST_DATABASE_URL override verified; Go skip line without Docker; CI/MAVERICK_TEST_REQUIRE_DB turns skip into failure; orphaned containers reaped by label+pid. Package 2b wires Schema::sqlx(&MIGRATOR).then(graphile_worker schema) when the migrations land.

title: Build shared test observability: per-test log capture, step logger, parity diff reporters, secret-leak check
description:
# What
Shared test observability so every failing test explains itself: a per-test tracing subscriber, a step logger for multi-step tests, and readable diffs for parity comparisons. Every package uses it. Polish-round requirement: "comprehensive unit tests and e2e test scripts with great, detailed logging."

# Features (in the parity-support dev crate or a sibling `test-support` crate)
- `init_test_tracing()`: installs a per-test `tracing` subscriber (for example via `tracing-test` or a custom capture layer) that records all engine log lines and spans at DEBUG, prints them only when the test fails, and honors `RUST_LOG` to narrow noise. Output format matches the engine's JSON log shape so production logs and test logs read the same.
- A redaction check in the capture layer: if a captured line contains a registered secret (test API keys, master keys, canary strings), fail the test. This makes every test a small G5 check for free.
- `step!("...")` macro/helper for multi-step tests (store tests, replay, e2e, acceptance): logs a numbered step with elapsed time, so a failure shows the last completed step.
- Parity diff helpers: for JSON, a field-path diff (`$.recommendations[1].score: expected 94.1, got 94.2`) with the fixture anchor (`fixtures/decision/rank.json#case-7`) and any D-row tag in the message; for bytes (wire bodies, SSE, rewritten bodies), a hex+text diff around the first mismatch; for floats, show both values in full precision and as f32 bits.
- Replay reporter: a summary table at the end of a replay run (total, passed, allowlisted by D-row, unexplained), plus one detailed block per unexplained diff with request, expected response, actual response.
- Conventions doc (`crates/test-support/README.md`): name tests with the parity tag, one assertion message per fixture case, never log prompt/corpus content.

# Done when
Helpers exist with their own tests, and at least one test per helper demonstrates the failure output. Commit.
close_reason: Built test-support crate: per-test tracing capture, G5 secret-leak guard, step! logging, JSON/bytes/float diff reporters, replay reporter; 21 tests green; fmt+clippy+workspace CI fast pass

title: OWNER: approve DIVERGENCES rows for proxy behaviors the plan requires but D1-D25 do not list
description:
# The gap
`reference/engine-reference.md` Part 6 §11, §13, §16, §17 lists proxy behaviors the master plan requires but that have NO row in `parity/DIVERGENCES.md` (D1 to D25). AGENTS.md: "Do not add a new intended difference yourself. Ask the owner. After approval, add a row to DIVERGENCES.md and update the spec." The proxy replay (`parity/fixtures/proxy/scenarios.json`) will show diffs for these, and without rows they count as bugs.

# Items needing a decision (each: approve a new D-row, or keep Go behavior)
1. Retry-After: Go ignores it (QUIRK 11: a 429 advances immediately). Plan §3.5 core: "respect Retry-After". Scenario `x_chat_429_advances`.
2. Telemetry batching: Go sends one batch per request, from a detached goroutine, no exit flush. Plan §3.5 core batcher: 10 s / 20 items / exit flush, per tenant key.
3. Proxy rate limits: Go has none. Plan §3.5: "tighter rate limits than the API", per tenant key.
4. Parameter normalization: Go has exactly two mappings (chat `reasoning_effort` xhigh -> high; messages `output_config.effort` xhigh -> max). Plan §3.5: "normalized to the nearest value the routed model accepts", catalog-driven.
5. Stripping `X-Maverick-API-Key` from upstream requests: Go forwards it (QUIRK 14). Plan §3.5: credentials never pass through. This is arguably inside D13 but is not spelled out.
6. OTel: Go hand-builds OTLP JSON; Rust uses tracing-opentelemetry with W3C trace context (D19 covers redaction, not the payload shape asserted by `otel_*` fixtures).
7. Any Go QUIRK in Part 6 §16 that the maverick-core chain executor would naturally change (for example QUIRK 9, mid-stream abort relayed as a clean end; QUIRK 12, a 502 written to a gone client).

# Agent guidance until answered
Build the proxy so each item is a small, isolated switch, and run the replay against Go behavior first. Do not ship the Rust behavior for an item without a row. The owner may approve all of them in one pass.

# Close when
The owner has decided each item, and approved rows are added to DIVERGENCES.md and the spec.
close_reason: Owner approved 2026-09-28: items 1,2,3,5,6 as planned; item 4 catalog-driven. Recorded as DIVERGENCES D26 (Retry-After), D27 (core batcher), D28 (per-tenant-key rate limit), D29 (catalog-driven normalization, Go mappings as fallback), D30 (strip X-Maverick-API-Key upstream), D31 (OTel via tracing-opentelemetry). Spec v1 §8.1 'Trial proxy behavior' added.

title: OWNER: pre-decide six predictable parity differences (identity headers, Q-P2, MCP Q7, health key, error tails, down migrations)
description:
# Purpose
Pre-decide the parity differences the agents can already predict, so no package closeout stalls waiting for the owner mid-stream. AGENTS.md: only the owner adds DIVERGENCES rows. Each item below comes from a bead that currently says "ask the owner if a fixture pins this". This bead blocks nothing; if it is still open when an agent hits one of these diffs, the agent keeps Go behavior where feasible and lists the diff in the package closeout as pending this bead.

# Candidates (approve a row, or require Go behavior)
1. SDK/runtime identity headers. Go provider SDKs sent `User-Agent: Anthropic/Go 1.56.0`, `X-Stainless-*` headers, and the Go proxy's transport sent `User-Agent: Go-http-client/1.1` and `Accept-Encoding: gzip` (with transparent gunzip). Proposed row: Rust sends only the headers the provider APIs require plus an honest MM User-Agent; identity headers are not reproduced. (Beads 4.2, 4.3, 4.4, 6.6.)
2. Anthropic pre-send refusal (QUIRK Q-P2). The Go SDK refused `max_tokens > 21333` (and > 8192 for some Opus 4 ids) before sending, then retried 3 times with zero HTTP calls. Options: reproduce the check exactly, or a row saying the Rust client sends the request and lets the API decide. (Bead 4.2.)
3. MCP argument-validation error wording (QUIRK Q7). Go SDK text such as `validating "arguments": validating root: unexpected additional properties ["model"]`. Options: reproduce the wording with a formatter, or a row saying Rust keeps the tool-error shape and the `validating "arguments": ` prefix but not the library wording. (Bead 5.13.)
4. Health component under graphile_worker (D22 extension). Keep the JSON key `river_queues` and the statuses `no_workers|paused|stale|ok`, with details derived from graphile_worker; the `paused` status may never occur. Confirm that keeping the Go key name is wanted. (Bead 5.12.)
5. Error-text tails from Go libraries beyond D24/D25: capture decrypt errors (`tracing: decrypting capture %s: <gcm error>`), prompt assembly JSON errors (`parsing attachments: <json err>`, `parsing settings: <json err>`). Proposed row: same prefix, status, and code; library-specific tail text not reproduced (like D25). (Beads 2.23, 4.6.)
6. Store test `TestMigrationsUpDownUpClean`: sqlx baseline without a down migration. Proposed row: replaced by "up twice is a no-op" plus the schema comparison; down migrations are not shipped. (Bead 3.7.)

# Close when
The owner has decided each item; approved rows are added to `parity/DIVERGENCES.md` (D32 onward) and the spec where relevant.

Owner note: the Go implementation was never shipped.
