title: OWNER: confirm the debug replay rules for zero-retention tenants (D2) and the classifier budget on replay (D4)
description:
# Question for the owner

Bead 5.9 (8bd3b2b) implemented `POST /v1/debug/replay/{capture_id}`. Two replay rules are not written in the spec, the reference, or DIVERGENCES.md. Please confirm them or choose otherwise.

1. **Zero retention on replay.** A capture can exist for a tenant that turned zero retention on after the capture was made (window creation is refused for zero-retention tenants, so this is the only way). Go replayed on the default classifier column in that case. Rust applies D2 to the replay:
   - the prompt goes only to `classifier.zero_retention_column`, and only while that column has valid zero-retention evidence;
   - otherwise it goes to no column, and the replay answers `method: fallback_default` (200) without any call.
   The fail-closed zero-retention rule has priority, and D2 says the prompt never leaves the engine. The alternative would be a 409 or 422 error in that case.
2. **The classifier budget on replay.** A replay is a paid classifier call. Rust counts it against the tenant's daily quota and the global daily spend cap (D4), and records its spend. Past either limit, the replay answers the fallback.

# If confirmed

Add a note to the D2 and D4 rows in `parity/DIVERGENCES.md` (replay follows the same rules), and a sentence to spec §9.8. No code change is needed.

# If not

Tell the 5.9 owner (TealHarbor) which behavior you want; the code is in `crates/maverick-api/src/classify.rs` (`Resolver::replay`) and `crates/maverick-api/src/debug.rs`.

title: OWNER: decide whether to keep or replace the existing Go-era database
description:
# The decision
Keep the Go-era Postgres database (it holds one real benchmark) or start fresh.

# Consequences
- KEEP: the go-live step runs `maverick migrate adopt-goose-baseline` (verifies the live schema fingerprint and transactionally inserts the exact `_sqlx_migrations` row so sqlx checksum validation passes), seeds `batches` with completed rows for every (kind, window) that already has `runs`, and the first live Rust nightly must pass pre-registered distribution checks against the stored Go aggregates (mean paired delta per provider and per capability within one pooled standard error; at most 5% of cells outside max(2 sigma, 2 points) with variance floored at 2 points; no regression alert attributable to the port; spend within 10% of projection). River tables stay untouched until 30 days after cutover (D22). Migrations stay additive during the rollback window (D21).
- REPLACE: fresh `maverick migrate`; no adopt command needed at go-live (still build it, it is part of the plan), no distribution comparison.

# Close when
The owner decides. Record the choice in the close reason.
close_reason: Owner 2026-09-28: START FRESH. Rust gets a new empty database at go-live. No adopt-goose-baseline run, no batches backfill, no River tables to keep, no Go-vs-Rust distribution checks. The one Go-era benchmark is not carried over.

title: OWNER: set default classifier daily quota and global classifier spend cap
description:
# The decision
Default values for `MAVERICK_CLASSIFIER_DAILY_QUOTA` (per-tenant daily classification quota) and `MAVERICK_CLASSIFIER_DAILY_SPEND_CAP_USD` (global daily classifier spend cap). The spec says "set from M6 cost measurement" (spec §14.1, master plan §3.1 "Classifier budget").

# Background
The prompt path puts an MM-paid classifier call on every cache miss, and the cache is exact-match, so unique prompts nearly always miss. D4 adds the budget: past either limit the request degrades to `fallback_default` with a `classification_quota_exceeded` flag instead of spending. M6 success criterion: classifier cost under 10% of plan price at P95 usage. Operators override per tenant via `PUT /internal/v1/tenants/{id}/limits`.

# Agent guidance until answered
Implement the mechanism with the values required by config (no invented numbers baked in as defaults unless the spec gives one). Tests set explicit values. Do not pick production defaults yourself.

title: Package 2a: Pure domain crates (ids, tasks, graders, scoring, ranking, policy, ceilings, alias, crypto)
description:
# Goal
Port every pure (no I/O, no SQL) piece of engine logic into domain crates, gated by the fixture files in `parity/fixtures/`. HANDOFF §4 row 2a; master plan §7.0 step 2(a). Reference Parts 2, 3, 4.

# Scope
IDs (prefix + ULID), task and grader types (serde tagged enums), the corpus file loader and validator, the grader framework and the five grader kinds (JSON schema, rule scan, golden answer, key facts, judge rubric; test_suite is reserved and rejected), scoring (run quality, high-stakes overlay, variance and ambiguity penalties, judge order swap, cell observation, availability, censored latency), EWMA + Welford, regression detection math, prediction/Brier/overconfidence math, spend projection math, ranking (modes, bands, noise band, same-family tie bias, availability floor), ceilings and banded policy, policy engine (pool, allowlist, standing constraints incl. zero retention, request preferences, G4 simulation/validation), check specs and reasons, alias grammar, workload projection, capture crypto and fingerprints, API key format and hashing, classifier pure logic (prompt text, parse, truncation, degraded tracker), telemetry outcome derivation, catalog lifecycle logic.

# Why a separate package
These are the numbers the product sells. They must match Go bit-for-bit where fixtures demand it (float32 storage widening, map-order summation at 1e-12), and `cargo-mutants` must run on them. Keeping them pure makes that fast and lets 2a run in parallel with 2b and 2c.

# Parity rules for every child
- Write the Rust tests from the fixture file first, then the code.
- Each Go test named in `parity/manifest/<area>.json` for the child's area needs a Rust test that replaces it (or a DIVERGENCES row). Name the Rust test so the manifest checker can map it.
- Before asserting, read `parity/DIVERGENCES.md`. If a row applies (D1, D5, D6, D7, D8, D9, D14, D16, D18, D24, D29, D36 touch this package), assert the Rust expected column, not the recorded Go value.
- Go regex `\d \w \s \b` are ASCII-only and Go lowercases per rune. Use `(?-u:\w)` style ASCII classes and per-char lowercasing where fixtures need Go results (reference Part 2 §15).
- Postgres `real` columns are float32; many expected values are float32 widened to float64. The reference marks each one.
- Six property tests used Go's RNG; implement them as properties (proptest or similar), not as replayed streams.
- Serde enums for tagged unions: an unknown variant fails at deserialization; a missing match arm fails at compile time.

# Done when
All child beads closed, all `parity/fixtures/{decision,measurement-io,measurement-core}` pure fixtures pass, `cargo-mutants` runs clean (or survivors are justified) on the domain crates, clippy clean.

title: Port the variance penalty, ambiguity penalty, and judge order-swap folding
description:
# What
The variance penalty over repeats, the ambiguity penalty over shared dimensions, and the judge order-swap folding. Spec §6.2, §6.3; reference Part 3 §1.

# Formulas
Variance (over repeats that produced gradable output; runner.repeats = 3):
- `mu = mean(q_run)`, `sigma = stddev(q_run)` (sigma = 0 when only one gradable repeat; check the reference for population vs sample stddev and match Go).
- `task_score = max(0, mu - lambda_var * sigma)`, `lambda_var = 0.5` (config `MAVERICK_SCORING_LAMBDA_VAR`).
- Missing repeats (errors, timeouts) do not enter mu but are recorded. A pair with zero gradable repeats contributes no task score and counts against availability (D6).

Ambiguity:
- When two or more graders score the same output on the same task dimension (via `weight_dimensions`), `a_output = stddev(scores for the shared dimension on this output)`; `a = mean(a_output over repeats)`.
- `task_score = max(0, task_score - lambda_amb * a)`, `lambda_amb = 0.25` (config `MAVERICK_SCORING_LAMBDA_AMB`).
- Judge order-swap disagreement is folded into `a_output` as two observations of the judge's dimension.
- Cells also aggregate `a` as the `ambiguity` dimension.

# Parity gate
`parity/fixtures/measurement-core/penalties.json` (12 rows) and `orderswap.json` (9 rows).

# Done when
All rows pass at the reference's stated tolerance. Mutants clean. Commit.
close_reason: Completed: scoring::penalties (variance_penalty, shared_dimension_spread, ambiguity, ambiguity_penalty, order_swap_observations, grader_observations folding). All 21 penalties/orderswap rows + extras tagged; 0 missed mutants.

title: Port cell observation, EWMA + Welford fold, availability (D6), censored latency (D7), measured flag
description:
# What
Cell observation per batch, the new availability dimension, censored latency percentiles, the EWMA fold with Welford variance, and the `measured` flag. Spec §6.4; reference Part 3 §1. The DB-backed `aggregate_rebuild` job that calls this is in package 2e.

# Formulas
- Cell = (column, capability, difficulty tier). Observation `x_t(cell) = mean(task_score over the cell's tasks in this batch)`.
- Dimensions per cell per batch: `quality` (gradable runs only; stored in [0,1], displayed x100 with one decimal), `pass_rate` (fraction of task-repeats passing; errors and timeouts count as failures), `ambiguity`, `latency_p50_ms`, `latency_p95_ms`, `cost_per_run_usd` (mean), `availability` (NEW).
- EWMA per (cell, dimension), seeded by the first observation: `S_0 = x_0`; `S_t = alpha * x_t + (1 - alpha) * S_{t-1}`, alpha = 0.3 (`MAVERICK_SCORING_ALPHA`).
- `aggregates.variance` is the running Welford variance of the x_t series (used by regression scan). `n` counts observations. `measured = (n >= scoring.min_nights)`, default 3 (`MAVERICK_SCORING_MIN_NIGHTS`). The plan phrases this as "3 distinct nights"; confirm with the reference whether n counts nights or observations and match Go.
- Smoke and sweep observations feed the same EWMA stream.

# Divergences
- D6: new per-cell `availability` = fraction of every scheduled repeat in the cell (including timeouts and provider errors) that returned output. Go has no such dimension.
- D7: latency percentiles include each timeout, censored at the timeout value. Go folded latency only from runs with a measured latency. Assert the Rust rule and tag D7 where a Go fixture differs.

# Float32 (critical for parity)
Postgres stores `real` as float32. The Go fold read float32 values, computed in float64, and stored float32. Fixtures are "bit-exact under float32 storage" (plan §7.0 step 2(e)). Reproduce the same widen/narrow points exactly; the reference marks each value.

# Parity gate
`parity/fixtures/measurement-core/observe.json` (4 rows) and `ewma.json` (5 rows). Property: EWMA convergence (spec §15), written as a property test.

# Done when
All rows pass bit-exact where required. Mutants clean. Commit.
close_reason: Completed: scoring::observe (Observe, nearest-rank percentile, D6 availability, D7 censored timeouts via RunStats::from_run) and scoring::ewma (Stream fold/resume/variance/measured, fold_observation bit-exact through f32 storage). 9 observe/ewma rows + extras tagged; EWMA convergence proptest; 0 missed mutants.

title: Port regression-detection math and the parse-failure watch
description:
# What
The pure math of regression detection and the parse-failure watch. The `regression_scan` job that reads aggregates and writes alerts is in package 2e. Spec §6.5, §11; reference Part 3 §1 and §2.

# Rules
- Smoothed drop: `S_t < max(S over trailing 7 days) - 3.0` (quality points on the 0 to 100 scale).
- Raw shock: `x_t < S_{t-1} - max(2 * sqrt(variance), 3.0)`.
- Severity: warning; critical if the cell's column is in any tenant pool AND the drop crosses that tenant's quality bar.
- Dedupe: one alert per cell per 7 days unless the drop deepens by >= 2 further points (re-arm).
- Parse-failure watch: a column's batch parse-failure rate > 5% AND > 2x its trailing 7-day rate raises `parse_failure_rate` (the leading indicator of caller-side silent escalation).

# Parity gate
`parity/fixtures/measurement-core/regression.json` (8 rows). Given/when/then cases that need DB state are in reference Part 3 §6 and belong to the regression_scan job bead.

All rows pass. Mutants clean. Commit.

title: Port request-time policy evaluation (pool, allowlist, standing constraints, preferences) with D1 zero retention
description:
# What
Request-time policy evaluation: the fixed five-step order that turns a pool into ranked survivors, recording every exclusion with a closed-enum reason. Spec §7.1, §7.3, §7.5; reference Part 4 §1 "policy" (exact error strings, order, reason spellings).

# Order of operations
1. Pool restriction (G2). `request.pool` by name, else the tenant's default. Unknown pool -> `422 unknown_pool`. Candidates = pool columns minus retired. A request can narrow a pool; it can never widen it.
2. Allowlist (G3). Each `allowed_models` entry resolves against the SYSTEM catalog. No match -> `422 unknown_model` naming the entry. Resolves but not in pool -> `422 model_not_in_pool` naming the entry. An entry matches a column when it equals the column `model_id` (all endpoint/settings variants in the pool) or the column `id` (exact).
3. Standing constraints: tenant `max_cost_per_run` vs `cost_per_run_usd` EWMA, `max_latency_ms` vs `latency_p95_ms` EWMA. Hard filters. If drift has emptied the set, keep least-violating columns, flag `constraints_met: false`, and fire a `pool_would_be_empty` critical alert (G1 outranks these two filters).
4. Request preferences (per-request `constraints`): stable partition into satisfying and violating; violators sort after satisfiers everywhere and are never dropped. If the pick violates one: `constraints_met: false` plus `violations[]` entries like `{"constraint": "max_latency_ms", "limit": 2000, "estimated": 3400}`.
5. Rank (ranking bead).
Score inputs (§7.3): a candidate with no aggregate row for the cell is excluded `no_data`, unless that empties survivors; then unmeasured candidates stay in with `measured: false` (G1).

# Exclusion reasons (closed enum, serde)
`not_in_pool`, `not_in_allowlist`, `standing_constraint:max_cost_per_run`, `standing_constraint:max_latency_ms`, `standing_constraint:zero_retention` (new), `status_retired`, `no_data`.

# Divergence D1 (zero retention, new in Rust, privacy)
When the tenant's `zero_retention` constraint is set, exclude every candidate whose EFFECTIVE `retention_mode` is not `zero` with reason `standing_constraint:zero_retention`. Effective mode: `unknown | standard | zero`; only `zero` with an unexpired `retention_valid_until` counts; expired evidence reads as `unknown`. This fails CLOSED: never relaxed for G1. If it empties the set: `409 no_compliant_columns`, nothing recommended, critical `pool_would_be_empty` alert naming tenant and pool. Least-violating relaxation of cost/latency draws only from zero-compliant columns. Go ignored the flag here (it only blocked debug capture).

# Parity gate
`parity/fixtures/decision/policy_evaluate.json` (13 rows), `policy_reasons.json` (1), `policy_property_g1.json` (1; the G1 property "survivors never empty after policy on a validated config", implemented as a property test), `reasons.json`. Plus new Rust tests for D1 (retention expiry yields 409, never stale compliance; `unknown` never satisfies zero retention).

# Rule
No SQL in this crate. Inputs are plain structs (tenant config, pool, catalog, aggregates, clock for expiry).

# Done when
All rows pass, D1 tests added, mutants clean. Commit.
close_reason: Policy evaluate + D1 ported; 31/31 unit and 600/600 G1 fixture cases match Go; D1 tests; mutants clean (66 caught, 10 unviable; equivalent min-fold mutant removed)

title: Port G4 write-time simulation and config validation (incl. zero retention)
description:
# What
G4 "no empty configurations": the simulation that checks every pool, under the constraints as they would exist after a write, against current aggregates, keeps at least one usable column. The same function backs config writes, the internal seam, the retirement guard, and the nightly drift check. Spec §7.2; reference Part 4 §1 (exact error strings, which pool and constraint get named).

# Rules
- `PUT /v1/config/pools` and `PUT /v1/config/constraints` (and their internal-seam twins) validate TOGETHER before commit: for every pool as it would exist after the write, applying the standing constraints as they would exist after the write, against CURRENT aggregates, must leave >= 1 non-retired column. Violation -> `422 pool_would_be_empty` naming the pool and the constraint that empties it; nothing is written.
- Zero retention (D1) is part of the simulation: with it set, every pool must keep >= 1 column with valid (unexpired) zero-retention evidence.
- Weight writes validate `w_q + w_c + w_l = 1` (+/- 0.001) and `0 < quality_bar <= 1`.
- Drift check: a pool within one column of empty raises a `pool_would_be_empty` warning.
- An internal column write that downgrades retention runs the simulation and raises a critical `pool_would_be_empty` alert naming each zero-retention tenant it would empty. The write is NOT blocked (retention is evidence about the provider, not tenant config).
- Request-body validation for config endpoints (`validate_input.json`).

# Parity gate

title: Port the ranking algorithm (modes, bands, noise-band ties, D8 availability floor, D9 entry fields)
description:
# What
The ranking algorithm over policy survivors, producing the pick (index 0) and the pool-constrained fallback chain. Spec §7.4; reference Part 4 §2 "recommend" (exact tie-break order, float handling, reason strings).

# Algorithm
Inputs per candidate: Q = quality EWMA x100, P = pass_rate EWMA, C = cost_per_run_usd EWMA, L = latency_p95_ms EWMA, A = mean availability over the trailing 7 nights, measured. Quality/pass come from `quality_source_column_id` when set (secondary endpoints borrow quality from their primary; latency and cost stay their own).
- Normalize over survivors only, per query, never stored: `nQ = minmax(Q)`, `nC = 1 - minmax(C)`, `nL = 1 - minmax(L)`. minmax over one survivor or equal values yields 1.0 for all.
- `V = w_q*nQ + w_c*nC + w_l*nL`. Default weights when the tenant has no `tenant_weights` row for the capability: quality 0.8/0.1/0.1, balanced 0.5/0.35/0.15, cost 0.25/0.6/0.15.
1. Band by mode: quality 0.0, balanced 1.5, cost 5.5 quality points (`MAVERICK_RANKING_BAND_*`). Leaders = `Q >= max(Q) - band`, within the preference-satisfying partition first.
2. Order leaders by V descending.
3. Append non-leaders by Q descending (the tail is a sane escalation chain).
4. Noise-band ties: adjacent candidates with `|Qi - Qj| <= 0.75` (`MAVERICK_RANKING_NOISE_BAND`) reorder cheaper C first; prefer a same-family (same provider) cheaper downgrade over a cross-family swap.
5. Preference violators sort after all satisfiers, ordered by the same rules.
6. D8 (new): candidates with A below the availability floor (default 0.9, `MAVERICK_RANKING_AVAILABILITY_FLOOR`) rank after every candidate at or above it, ordered by the same rules, and carry `low_availability: true`. Go had no availability input.

# Entry fields (D9)
Every chain entry carries its column's `settings` (reasoning effort, thinking mode) and its effective `retention_mode`, plus `low_availability`. Displayed `score` is absolute quality x100 with one decimal (`rank_extras.json` display_score); ranking normalization is never shown.

# Parity gate
`parity/fixtures/decision/rank.json` (4 rows), `rank_extras.json` (1 row: display_score, high_stakes), `rank_property.json` (3 property rows; implement as properties: normalization bounds, etc.). New tests for D8 ordering. Where Go fixtures lack `settings`/`retention_mode`/`low_availability`, assert the Rust shape and tag D8/D9.

# Done when
All rows pass, D8 tests added, mutants clean. Commit.
close_reason: Ranking ported with D8 availability floor and D9 entry fields; 20/20 rank.json and 2200/2200 rank_property.json bit-exact (Go fixtures were FMA-fused: V uses mul_add); rank_extras 22/22; mutants clean

title: Port difficulty ceilings, clears_difficulty, and the banded policy table
description:
# What
Difficulty ceilings, the per-entry `clears_difficulty` flag, and the banded policy table behind `GET /v1/policies`. Spec §6.6, §7.5, §9.3; reference Part 4 §2.

# Rules
- For column x capability at a tenant's quality bar B (default 0.80) with buffer beta = 0.05 (`MAVERICK_CEILING_BUFFER`): `ceiling = max { T in 1..5 : for all t <= T, ewma_pass_rate(t) >= B + beta }`, 0 if none. Watch float32: B and pass rates are stored as `real`; compare exactly as Go did.
- A column clears difficulty d iff `ceiling >= d`. A pick below the ceiling still returns, flagged `clears_difficulty: false`.
- Bands: easy 1-2, medium 3, hard 4-5. Per capability, the banded table lists the cheapest column in the pool whose ceiling >= the band's top tier. "Cheapest" = `cost_per_run_usd` EWMA averaged over the band's tiers.
- Unmeasured cells count as not clearing, except: if NOTHING in a pool clears a band, list the best available column with `clears_band: false` (G1 applied to policies).

# Parity gate
`parity/fixtures/decision/ceiling.json` (4 rows), `ceiling_property.json` (1 property row, band monotonicity; implement as a property), `bands.json` (9 rows).

# Done when
All rows pass. Mutants clean. Commit.

title: Port catalog lifecycle, retirement guard decision, quality transfer, and retention evaluation
description:
# What
Pure catalog logic: column lifecycle transitions, the retirement guard decision, retention-status evaluation, and quality transfer for secondary endpoints. The `catalog_sync` and `price_sync` jobs and the internal column endpoints that call this are in 2e and 2d. Spec §4.1 to §4.5; reference Part 3 §5 "internal/catalog".

# Rules
- A column is (provider, model, endpoint, settings). Thinking on and off are two columns. Columns are data, created and edited through the internal API, never seeded in migrations.
- Lifecycle `cold_start -> active -> deprecated -> retired`. A cold-start column runs the full corpus nightly for a dense-run window (default 5 nights, `MAVERICK_CATALOG_COLD_START_NIGHTS`); its cells report unmeasured until they have enough nights.
- Secondary-endpoint columns (`quality_source_column_id` set, for example a Vertex variant) borrow quality cells from their primary but keep their own latency (from hourly probes) and cost.
- Each column snapshots list price per million tokens. Run cost is computed from the snapshot at execution time and never restated.
- Retirement guard (G4): before any column retires, simulate every tenant pool containing it (uses the G4 simulation bead). A pool that would drop to zero BLOCKS the transition and raises a critical `pool_would_be_empty` alert.
- Retention (D1, spec §4.5): `retention_mode in unknown|standard|zero`, `retention_verified_at`, `retention_valid_until` (at most 90 days after verification; writes exceeding it are `422 invalid_request`), `retention_source` link. Expired evidence reads as `unknown` everywhere. The same rules apply per `execution_aliases` entry (stored in `model_columns.execution_alias_retention`). `catalog_sync` raises `retention_expiring` 14 days before any expiry.

# Parity gate
`parity/fixtures/measurement-core/catalog.json` (11 rows). New Rust tests for retention evaluation and expiry.

All rows pass, retention tests added, mutants clean. Commit.

title: Port the alias grammar into maverick-core (with D14 ?settings=caller)
description:
# What
The alias grammar, parsed identically everywhere (proxy, SDK cores, engine). Lives in `maverick-core` so the proxy and the conformance harness share one implementation. Reference Part 6 §5 (`ParseAlias`); master plan §3.5; spec §7.4 (settings opt-out).

# Go grammar (reproduce exactly)
Input: the raw `model` string. Output `{pool, mode}` or one of two errors.
1. Must start with the exact, case-sensitive prefix `maverick/`, else `not_maverick_alias`.
2. `rest` = everything after the prefix.
3. If `rest` contains `:`, split at the FIRST `:` into pool and modeWord; either part empty -> `malformed_alias`. Else pool = "" and modeWord = rest.
4. modeWord (exact, case-sensitive): `auto` -> balanced, `quality` -> quality, `cost` -> cost. Anything else (including `balanced`, `AUTO`, "", " auto") -> `malformed_alias`.
Consequences: pool is any non-empty string without `:` (spaces and `/` allowed, no trimming). `maverick/prod:pool:auto` is malformed. `maverick/auto:auto` is pool `auto`, mode balanced. Both error kinds map to the same HTTP 400 in the proxy.

# Divergence D14 (settings opt-out)
Rust adds the suffix `?settings=caller`, for example `maverick/<pool>:<mode>?settings=caller` (and presumably `maverick/auto?settings=caller`). Default: the proxy and SDK cores apply the recommended entry's `settings`; with the suffix they leave the caller's settings alone. In Go this string is `malformed_alias` (400). Tag the affected unit.json rows D14 and assert the Rust result. Keep the parse output struct explicit: `{pool: Option, mode, settings_mode: Apply|Caller}`.

# Other rule
A concrete model name where an alias is expected is rejected by the proxy (400) and passed through untouched by an SDK ("don't route, just call it"). The parser returns `not_maverick_alias`; the caller decides.

# Parity gate
`parity/fixtures/proxy/unit.json#parse_alias-*` rows (manifest `parity/manifest/proxy.json`). Conformance scenario 9 (alias table) reuses this.

# Done when
All parse_alias rows pass (D14 rows tagged), property test that parse never panics on arbitrary input. Commit.
close_reason: Ported alias grammar (ParseAlias) into maverick-core with D14 ?settings=caller; all 23 parse_alias-* parity rows pass plus a no-panic property test

title: Define and implement the versioned workload projection in maverick-core (D5)
description:
# What
The versioned workload projection (D5): one definition, shared by the proxy and every SDK core, that turns a chat request (OpenAI chat completions or Anthropic Messages) into the prompt text the classifier sees. Lives in `maverick-core`. Spec v1 §8.1 "Workload projection"; `plans/model-maverick-sdk-v0-plan.md` §2.1; master plan §3.5; reference Part 6 §6 (the Go rule being replaced).

# The Go rule (replaced; know it to read the fixtures)
`extractLastUserText`: decode `{messages:[{role, content}]}` (case-insensitive keys), walk from last to first, take the first `role == "user"` (case-sensitive), use its string content or the concatenation of `type == "text"` parts, cap at 100,000 Unicode scalar values. Empty -> declared fallback workload. No system prompt, no tools, no multi-turn context. Cases: `unit.json#extract_last_user_text-*`. These rows get a D5 tag and a Rust expected output.

# Required content (fixed by the spec)
- Include: system/developer instructions; bounded recent conversation text (not only the last user message); the response-format schema; tool names and descriptions.
- Exclude binary content (images, audio, file parts, and base64 payloads).
- Truncate per spec §8.3: oversize input uses head 80,000 + tail 20,000 Unicode scalar values; confidence is capped at 0.8 by the engine.
- A projection version string is sent as `workload.projection_version`; the engine folds it into the classification cache key.
- `X-Maverick-Workload: <capability>[:<tier>]` selects the declared form instead (Go forwarded that header upstream).

# The agent defines the exact format (no owner gate)
The spec fixes WHAT goes in, not the byte layout. The implementing agent defines the layout, names it version `p1`, and writes it down; it does not wait for approval, because the version is part of the cache key and a later change is a safe version bump. Required decisions, each written into a new "Projection format p1" paragraph in spec v1 §8.1 in the same commit:
- Section order and delimiters (suggested: `[system]`, `[response_format]`, `[tools]`, `[conversation]` headers, one blank line between sections; empty sections omitted).
- The "recent conversation" bound (suggested: the most recent messages, newest last, until 16,000 scalar values are used; always include the final user message in full up to the global cap).
- Role labels for each turn (suggested: `user:`, `assistant:`, `tool:`), how tool-call arguments and `tool_result` text appear (suggested: text included, JSON compacted), and how both surfaces (chat `messages` with `system`/`developer` roles, Messages top-level `system` string or blocks) map onto the same layout.
- Deterministic output: same input bytes -> same projection bytes, in every language.
The owner can review the written format at any time; review does not block this bead or its dependents.

# Tests (with detailed logging)
Golden `insta` fixtures for: single-turn, multi-turn, system + user, developer role, tool-use request with tool results, response_format schema, binary parts excluded, oversize truncation (both surfaces). On a mismatch the test prints the input, the expected and actual projection, and a diff. Export the same cases as conformance vectors (JSON) for the four SDKs. M6 gates on multi-turn and tool-use classification fixtures.

# Done when
Projection function + `p1` constant + spec paragraph + fixtures + vectors committed, D5 rows tagged. Commit.
close_reason: Projection p1 in maverick-core (project/project_value, PROJECTION_VERSION, parse_workload_header, RFC 8785 JCS); spec 8.1 'Projection format p1'; 16 insta goldens (both surfaces); 39 conformance vectors in crates/sdk-conformance/vectors/projection.p1.json; all 23 extract_last_user_text rows tagged D5 with Rust expected output

title: Port prompt fingerprint, capture crypto with D18 key ring, and the capture decision
description:
# What
The prompt fingerprint, the debug-capture crypto with the new key ring (D18), and the pure capture decision. Reference Part 4 §4.1, §4.2, §4.4, §4.5; spec §10.1, §10.4. The DB-backed capture flow (insert, replay, reads, access log) is in the API package.

# Fingerprint (G5, G6)
`"hmac_sha256:" + lowercase_hex(HMAC-SHA256(key = tenants.prompt_hmac_key (32 random bytes minted at tenant creation), message = the prompt's exact UTF-8 bytes))`. No normalization, no trimming (NFC and NFD differ). The same value is the classification cache key, the response `prompt_hash`, and the trace column.

# Capture crypto
- Master key: `MAVERICK_CAPTURE_MASTER_KEY`, exactly 64 hex chars = 32 bytes (config error text: `must be 64 hex characters encoding a 32-byte key`). Non-32-byte key at use: `tracing: capture master key must be 32 bytes, got %d`.
- Data key = HKDF-SHA256 (RFC 5869): IKM = master key, salt = UTF-8 bytes of the capture id (`cap_...`), info empty, length 32.
- AES-256-GCM, fresh 12-byte (96-bit) CSPRNG nonce per capture, no AAD, 16-byte tag appended. Stored: `ciphertext` = ct || tag, `nonce` = 12 bytes.
- Open failure: `tracing: decrypting capture %s: <gcm error>` (D36, owner-decided: keep the `tracing: decrypting capture <id>: ` prefix byte for byte; the tail after it is the Rust aead error text and is not compared).
- D18 key ring (new): current key (`MAVERICK_CAPTURE_MASTER_KEY`, version `MAVERICK_CAPTURE_MASTER_KEY_VERSION`, default 1) plus at most one previous key (`MAVERICK_CAPTURE_PREVIOUS_MASTER_KEY` as `version:hex`). Each capture stores `capture_key_version`. Encrypt only with the current key; decrypt by stored version. A retired key is dropped once `capture.max_window_minutes + capture.retention_hours` have passed since rotation.
- Use `subtle` for any secret comparison; zeroize keys in memory where practical.

# Capture decision (`Decide`)
`decide(windows, zero_retention, api_key_id, confidence, now)`: zero retention -> never. Else the first window in list order with `starts_at <= now < ends_at`, `api_key_id` null or equal, and `confidence_below` null or `confidence < confidence_below` (strict). No randomness. QUIRK: `confidence_below` is float32, so a window created with 0.95 compares against 0.949999988079071 (confidence 0.95 is NOT captured; 0.9499999 is). Reproduce.

# Parity gate
`parity/fixtures/decision/tracing_fingerprint.json` (7 rows; includes RFC 4231 test case 2, NFC vs NFD, empty prompt), `tracing_capture_crypto.json` (4 rows + fixed-nonce vectors), `tracing_capture_decide.json` (1 row + extra cases). New tests for the key ring: encrypt with v2, decrypt a v1 capture via previous key, reject unknown version, drop rule.

# Done when
All rows pass, key-ring tests added, mutants clean. Commit.
close_reason: Ported prompt fingerprint, capture crypto (HKDF+AES-256-GCM), D18 key ring, and capture decide; parity fixtures pass

title: Port API key minting/hashing and internal token parsing with constant-time match
description:
# What
Pure auth primitives: API key minting and hashing, and internal token parsing and constant-time matching. The axum middleware that uses them (and the rate limiter) is in the API package. Reference Part 4 §5.1 and §5.3; spec §9.1, §13.

# API keys
- Raw key = `mk_live_` + base62(32 CSPRNG bytes), always 43 chars after the prefix (51 total).
- base62: treat the 32 bytes as a big-endian unsigned integer; repeatedly divide by 62, remainders are digits (least significant first) from the alphabet `0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZabcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz`; left-pad with `0` to 43 digits; most significant first. 32 zero bytes -> 43 zeros.
- At rest: `key_hash = SHA-256(raw key string bytes, including the prefix)` (32 bytes, bytea); `last4` = last 4 chars of the raw key. The raw key is shown once and never stored.

# Internal tokens
- `MAVERICK_INTERNAL_TOKENS` (required): split on `,`, trim each entry, split at the FIRST `:` into label and secret (both non-empty; a secret may contain `:`), else config error `must be a comma-separated list of "label:secret" pairs`.
- At startup store `SHA-256(label + ":" + secret)` per entry. A request bearer is hashed and compared against EVERY entry with a constant-time compare over the 32-byte digests (all entries always compared; the first match's label wins). The label is recorded as the acting party.

# Parity gate
`parity/fixtures/decision/auth_keys.json` (4 rows). Manifest `decision.json` (auth package; the other auth rows that need a store are in the API auth-middleware bead).

# Done when
Rows pass; timing-safe comparison verified by using `subtle::ConstantTimeEq`. Commit.
close_reason: Ported API key mint/hash + internal token constant-time auth; parity auth_keys.json rows pass

# What

# Rules

title: Port the grader framework, spec envelope, registry, and golden-fixture harness
description:
# What
The grader trait and registry. Each kind exposes `kind()`, `validate_spec(spec)`, and `grade(spec, input) -> (dimension -> score in [0,1], detail JSON)`. The detail JSON is persisted to `scores.detail`. The spec envelope `{type, version, weight_dimensions, spec}` maps emitted dimensions onto task dimension names (multiplier per dimension, normally 1.0). Two graders MAY feed the same task dimension. This is what makes shared-dimension ambiguity measurable (spec §6.3).

# Key semantics (spec §5.2)
A grader ERROR (not a low score) marks the run's affected dimensions ABSENT and increments a grader-failure counter. It never silently scores 0. Absent dimensions are renormalized away in run quality (see the scoring bead).

# Parity gate
- `parity/fixtures/measurement-io/graders_framework.json` (20 manifest rows: `internal/graders/envelope_test.go` 11 + `grader_test.go` 9).

- Reference Part 2 §6 and §12.

# Design
Serde tagged enum for the envelope `type`, so an unknown kind fails at deserialization and a missing match arm fails at compile time. The judge grader needs a judge-call abstraction (a trait) that the fake provider implements in tests. Define that trait in the domain layer; do not depend on the real provider clients.

# Done when
Framework rows pass, and the harness is usable by the five grader-kind beads. Commit.

title: Port the judge_rubric grader (cross-family judge, order-swapped calls)
description:
# What
The `judge_rubric` grader: a cross-family judge scores the rubric dimensions (named by the rubric, for example `idiom`, `readability`, `overall`). Spec §5.5; reference Part 2 §11 has the exact judge prompt text, structured-output schema, parse rules, and error strings.

# Judge protocol
- Judge pool: two columns from different families, config `judge.pool` (seed `gemini-3.1-pro/direct`, `gpt-5.5/direct`; env `MAVERICK_JUDGE_POOL`). The judge for an output is the FIRST pool member whose family differs from the graded column's family, so every output is judged cross-family, including outputs from the judges' own families. Family = provider.
- Two structured-output calls per (output, rubric) at temperature 0, with rubric item order REVERSED on the second call. Per-dimension score = mean of the two. The absolute per-dimension disagreement feeds the ambiguity penalty (the order-swap bead folds it in).
- Inputs: task prompt, model output, rubric, and reference material (golden answer, reference solution). Judges see reference material; benchmarked models never do (G7).
- A judge call that fails after retries omits its dimensions for that run and increments the judge-failure counter. The batch-level alert (>= 10% judge failures raises a `job_failure` warning) is in the jobs package.

# Parity gate
`parity/fixtures/measurement-io/judge_rubric.json` (12 rows, `internal/graders/judgerubric/grader_test.go`), testdata under `testdata/internal/graders/judgerubric/`, schema `schemas/judgerubric.spec.schema.json`.

# Design
The grader calls the model through a judge-call trait (defined with the grader framework). Tests use a scripted fake. Real provider wiring happens in the runner/jobs packages. Prompt text is data: copy it byte for byte from the reference or fixtures.

# Done when
All rows pass. Mutants clean. Commit.

title: Port per-run quality, pass, and the high-stakes overlay (with D6 error rule)
description:
# What
Per-run quality and pass, including the high-stakes overlay. Spec §6.1; reference Part 3 §1 "internal/scoring".

# Formulas
- `q_run = sum_d w_d * s_d` over PRESENT dimensions, renormalized over present dimensions (absent = grader error). Weights come from `tasks.dimension_weights`.
- `pass = (q_run >= task.pass_threshold)`. Feeds pass rates, ceilings, and prediction scoring.
- Truncated or refused outputs (`parse_failure`) are graded on whatever text exists; they count toward the column's parse-failure rate.
- High-stakes overlay (medical, legal, financial tags): weights are replaced by accuracy 0.40, calibration 0.20, hedging 0.15, citation honesty 0.25 (check the reference and `overlay.json` for the exact dimension names and mapping), and a failed `critical` rule or an `autofail` fact forces the run to fail (`q_run = 0`).

# Divergence D6 (important)
Go: provider errors and timeouts "score zero" (`q_run = 0`). Rust: a run with status `provider_error` or `timeout` has NO `q_run`. It is excluded from quality, counts as `pass = false` in pass rate (errors stay in the pass-rate denominator, so ceilings still penalize them), and counts against the new `availability` aggregate. Where a Go fixture asserts `q_run = 0` for an error run, assert the Rust rule and tag D6.

# Parity gate
`parity/fixtures/measurement-core/run_quality.json` (8 rows) and `overlay.json` (16 rows). Manifest `parity/manifest/measurement-core.json` (scoring package).

# Done when
All rows pass (with D6 tags where applicable). Mutants clean. Commit.

title: Port corpus subcommands: load, activate, status, calibrate report
description:
# What
The `maverick corpus` subcommands: `load`, `activate`, `status`, `calibrate`. Reference Part 1 §7.5 (every string, stream, and exit code is exact); fixture `parity/fixtures/store/calibrate.json` (10 rows from `cmd/maverick/calibrate_test.go`, 8 tests) and the corpus rows of `cli.json`.

# Key behavior
- `corpus` alone: corpus usage to stderr, exit 2. Unknown: `maverick corpus: unknown subcommand "<x>"` + blank line + usage, exit 2. Usage text is exact in the reference.
- Shared DB helper: logger to stdout; load config (exit 1); signal context; connect then ping (unreachable DB fails here with ERROR `connecting to database`, exit 1).
- `load --version --dir [--description] [--strict]`: missing version or dir -> stderr message, exit 2. Load and validate BEFORE config and DB (works with no env). `--strict` turns corpus-shape warnings (20-25 tasks, exactly 5 smoke members per capability) into errors. Warnings print first (`warning: <w>`), then errors (`error: <v>`), then `maverick corpus load: rejected <dir>: <n> violation(s)`, exit 1. On success stdout exactly: ``loaded corpus version <v>: <n> tasks (inactive; run `maverick corpus activate --version <v>`)``.
- `activate --version`: success `corpus version <v> is now active`; unknown version error text exact.
- `status`: Go tabwriter layout (min width 2, tab width 4, padding 2, spaces, last cell not padded). Header `VERSION  TASKS  ACTIVE  CREATED`; created_at in UTC RFC3339. Write a tiny tabwriter-compatible formatter.
- `calibrate`: operator report, never a gate (exit 0 whenever the DB is reachable). Drop unmeasured rows; group by (capability, column); sort by tier; `pts(x) = float64(float32 ewma) * 100`. INVERSION when a harder tier's pts is strictly greater than the easier tier's. OUTLIER when an interior tier deviates from the linear interpolation of its neighbors by more than 15.0 (strict). All inversions then outliers, then a STABLE sort by tier. Printing uses Go `%.1f` (round-half-to-even on the exact binary value; Rust `{:.1}` rounds differently on ties; test the tie cases). Corpus loader (2a), corpus persistence (2b), aggregates and model_columns queries, CLI dispatch.

title: Implement maverick serve wiring: startup order, three process shapes, graceful shutdown
description:
# What
`maverick serve` wiring: startup order, listeners, process shapes, and graceful shutdown. Reference Part 1 §7.3 (exact order and log messages); master plan §4 (three shapes: `serve`, `serve --api-only` stateless replica, `serve --worker-only` exactly one).

# Order (Go, reproduce unless a DIVERGENCES row applies)
1. Flags `--api-only`, `--worker-only`; both set -> ERROR `serve: --api-only and --worker-only are mutually exclusive`, exit 2 (before config).
2. Load config (exit 1 on failure). INFO `starting maverick` with `public_addr`, `internal_addr`, `api_only`, `worker_only`.
3. Signal context (SIGINT, SIGTERM).
4. Create the DB pool lazily (an unreachable DB does not fail startup).
5. Provider clients for each provider with a non-empty key, in order anthropic, openai, xai, google. Google client failure logs and continues.
6. Alert fan-out (shared by workers and API). Failure exits 1.
7. Unless `--api-only`: grader registry (judge_rubric only if the judge pool resolves; else ERROR `judge pool unavailable; judge_rubric gradings will fail until it resolves` and continue), job client (cron parse errors exit 1), start workers, INFO `workers started`.
8. Unless `--worker-only`: classifier resolver; failure logs `classifier column unavailable; prompt-path requests will receive the fallback classification` and continues.
9. Listeners: internal ALWAYS (so `--worker-only` still serves health and operator surfaces), public unless `--worker-only`; internal first. INFO `listening` with `listener` and `addr`. Read header timeout 10 s.
10. Wait for the signal (INFO `shutdown signal received`, code 0) or the first listener failure (ERROR `listener failed`, code 1).
11. Shutdown with one 10-second deadline: graceful shutdown of each HTTP server, then stop workers, then wait for in-flight alert deliveries (drain the process-wide fan-out). INFO `stopped`.

# Shutdown of running jobs (QUIRK J9, covered by D10/D11)
In Go the River client got the signal context, so SIGTERM hard-cancelled running jobs, and a partial batch finished its tail and was never retried. The Rust design replaces this under D10 (batches lease, resume) and D11 (transactional failure tail): on SIGTERM, stop taking new jobs, let running handlers reach a safe point within the shared shutdown deadline, and do NOT mark an unfinished batch completed. Its `runs` stay, its lease expires or is recovered, and the next delivery resumes it under the same batch id. Tag the J9-related tests D10/D11. No further owner approval is needed.

# Also
Startup rejects a batch lease TTL that is not shorter than graphile_worker's earliest recovery threshold (spec §11.2). OTel exporter setup (fail-open; no public metrics endpoint).

# Depends on

title: Implement the hidden maverick demo-run command
description:
# What
The hidden `maverick demo-run` command (phase-0 check). Reference Part 1 §7.6.

# Behavior
Flags `--seed` (default `scripts/demo/seed.sql`) and `--fake-fixtures` (default `scripts/demo/fixtures`). Load config, signal context, migrate (ERROR `migrate failed`, exit 1). New pool; execute the seed file as one multi-statement exec; build the fake provider from the fixture dir and register it for all four providers; list active tasks (none -> error `seed fixture <path> produced no active tasks`); runnable columns from the catalog (none -> `seed fixture <path> produced no runnable columns`); run ONE batch with the configured repeats, timeout, provider limits, and `MatrixVersion = tasks[0].corpus_version`; list runs by batch (none -> `batch <id> persisted no runs`). Output: `batch <bat_id>: <total> runs (<ok count> ok)` then a tabwriter table `RUN ID  STATUS  LATENCY_MS  TOKENS_IN  TOKENS_OUT  COST_USD` (NULL ints print empty, cost `%.6f`, empty when NULL).

# Why it matters
It is the M0 acceptance: a runner that executes a task against a column and stores a run, with no real provider. It is also a quick smoke check for the whole measurement path.

# Check first
Confirm `scripts/demo/seed.sql` and `scripts/demo/fixtures` exist in this repo (`scripts/` holds demo seed data). If the seed SQL targets the Go schema only, it must still work on the Rust schema (additive changes only).

# Depends on
Runner and fake provider (2c), store, CLI dispatch.

# Done when
The demo-run rows of `cli.json` (if any) pass and a test runs demo-run against testcontainers Postgres. Commit.

title: Write the up-only additive migrations (batches, retention, param_constraints, capture_key_version, outcomes CHECK, limits, budget counters, cache key, telemetry opt-out)
description:
# What
The up-only sqlx migrations on top of the baseline that bring the schema to the spec v1 §3 DDL for the Rust port (21 tables), plus the columns added by owner decisions on 2026-09-28. The baseline itself (equal to the Go goose head, `parity/schema/schema.sql`) is a separate bead.

# Rules
- Up only (D37): no `.down.sql` files.
- Additive in effect: add tables, add columns, widen CHECK sets. Never drop, rename, or narrow. (The owner chose a fresh database, so there are no existing rows to backfill; new NOT NULL columns need no backfill default unless the spec gives one.)
- One migration file per logical change, with a header comment naming the spec section and D-row.

# Contents
1. `batches` table (spec §3, D10): `id text primary key` (`bat_...`, deterministic per (kind, batch_window), equals `runs.batch_id` for batch kinds), `kind text not null`, `batch_window text not null` (not `window`, a reserved word), `status text not null default 'running' check (status in ('running','completed','skipped'))`, `lease_owner text`, `lease_expires_at timestamptz`, `heartbeat_at timestamptz`, `attempt int not null default 1`, `completed_at timestamptz`, `created_at`/`updated_at timestamptz not null default now()`, `unique (kind, batch_window)`.
2. `model_columns` retention (spec §4.5, D1, D15): `retention_mode` (`unknown|standard|zero`, default `unknown`), `retention_verified_at`, `retention_valid_until`, `retention_source`, and `execution_alias_retention` jsonb (per-alias retention, openrouter spec §2.1). Confirm `settings` and `execution_aliases` already exist in the baseline (Go 0001/0002).
3. `model_columns.param_constraints` jsonb not null default '{}' (D29; shape defined in bead 6.14, coordinate with it; if 6.14's design is not ready, ship this column in a later migration from that bead instead).
4. `debug_captures.capture_key_version int not null` (D18).
5. `outcomes.outcome` CHECK widened to allow `completed_unchecked` (D16): drop and re-add the constraint with the larger set.
6. Tenant limits for `classification_daily_quota` (spec §13 `PUT /internal/v1/tenants/{id}/limits`, D4), where the spec places them (a nullable override; null = engine default).
7. Classifier budget usage counters in Postgres (D4): per tenant per UTC day count, and global per UTC day spend, updated atomically so API replicas share them (no Redis). Table shape is the agent's choice; document it in spec §3.
8. `classification_cache` key includes the workload projection version (D5): add a `projection_version` column to the key (or fold it into the version string; pick one, document it in spec §8.3, and keep the store bead 3.6 consistent).
9. `tenant_constraints.telemetry_opt_out boolean not null default false` (D39, bead 5.19).
Data that needs no DDL: the `availability` dimension (a value of `aggregates.dimension`), `settings_applied` (in `outcomes.details`).

# Tests (real Postgres, detailed logging)
- All migrations on an empty database produce the expected objects (assert each column, type, default, constraint, and index by querying `information_schema`/`pg_catalog`); failures print the expected vs actual catalog rows.
- A second run applies nothing (D37).
- CHECK widening: inserting `completed_unchecked` succeeds; an unknown outcome still fails.
- `batches` unique constraint rejects a duplicate (kind, batch_window).

# Done when
Migrations committed with header comments, spec §3 updated for the objects it did not already define, tests pass. Commit.

# What
Port the store queries for measurement: `parity/schema/queries/runs.sql`, `scores.sql`, `aggregates.sql`, `predictions.sql`, `calibration.sql`, plus NEW queries for the `batches` table. Reference Part 7 and `parity/schema/queries.md`.

- Claim: insert-if-absent with deterministic id, status running, lease_owner = worker id, lease_expires_at, attempt 1; or take over when the lease expired or the owner is gone (attempt + 1). Must be race-safe under concurrent claimers: use `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (kind, batch_window) DO UPDATE ... WHERE <takeover condition> RETURNING`, or `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` in one transaction. Report which outcome happened (claimed, took over, completed/skipped no-op, live foreign lease no-op).
- Heartbeat: renew `lease_expires_at` and `heartbeat_at` only if still the owner.
- Complete and skip: set status, completed_at, clear the lease, only if still the owner.
- Read by (kind, window) for tests and health.

# Tests
Store tests on real Postgres, including a concurrency test where two tasks claim the same (kind, window) and exactly one wins.

All queries exist with tests. Commit.

title: Port corpus persistence and atomic activation (tasks store tests)
description:
# What
Persist and activate corpus versions. Reference Part 1 §3 (transaction boundaries) and Part 2 §13 (tasks store); spec §5.6.

# Transactions (exact)
- Store (corpus load): pre-checks outside the tx (version non-empty, corpus has at least one task). Then one transaction: `UpsertCorpusVersion(active=false)` -> `UpsertTask` per task in corpus order -> `DeactivateCorpusTasksNotIn(version, all task ids)` -> commit. Roll back on any error.
- Activate: one transaction: `AcquireCorpusActivationLock(0x6d76636f7270)` (a transaction-scoped advisory lock) -> `ActivateCorpusVersion(version)` -> commit. Zero rows affected -> `ErrUnknownVersion` with text `tasks: activate "<v>": unknown corpus version`, and roll back.
- Activation flips atomically; the system stays live throughout.

# Parity gate
`parity/manifest/measurement-io.json` rows from `internal/tasks/store_test.go` (9 tests), given/when/then in reference Part 2 §13. Real Postgres.

# Privacy
Tests use the synthetic YAML under `parity/fixtures/measurement-io/testdata/internal/tasks/` and `parity/fixtures/api/testdata/e2e_corpus/`. Never the private corpus.

# Done when
All 9 rows pass. Commit.

title: Port the maverick CLI: dispatch, Go-compatible flags, usage text, exit codes, JSON logging
description:
# What
The `maverick` binary's command dispatch, usage text, flag parsing, exit codes, and JSON logging. Reference Part 1 §7.1 and §7.2; fixture `parity/fixtures/store/cli.json` (20 manifest rows from `cmd/maverick/main_test.go`, 19 tests).

# Dispatch (exact)
`run(args, lookup, stdout, stderr) -> exit code`, so tests can drive it without a process.
- no args: main usage to stderr, exit 2.
- `serve [--api-only] [--worker-only]`, `migrate`, `demo-run` (hidden, not in usage), `corpus <load|activate|status|calibrate>`, `mcp-stdio --api-key <key>`.
- anything else: stderr `maverick: unknown command "<arg>"` + blank line + main usage, exit 2.
- Main usage text is exact (in the reference and fixture); it ends with a newline and has no demo-run line.

# Flags (Go `flag` semantics to reproduce)
Both `-flag` and `--flag`, `--flag=value` or `--flag value`, booleans take no value. Parse error or `-h`/`--help` prints `Usage of <set name>:` plus the flag list to stderr and returns 2. Flag set names: `serve`, `migrate`, `demo-run`, `mcp-stdio`, `corpus load`, `corpus activate`, `corpus status`, `corpus calibrate`. Positional args after flags are ignored. Exact help text for `serve -h` and the unknown-flag message are in `cli.json`. clap will not reproduce Go's output by default: either write a small Go-compatible flag parser or configure clap heavily. A hand-written parser is likely simpler and exact.

# Logging
JSON lines to stdout (INFO and above): `{"time":"<RFC3339Nano local>","level":"INFO|WARN|ERROR","msg":"...",<attrs in call order>}`; durations as integer nanoseconds; errors as strings. `mcp-stdio` logs to STDERR (stdout is the MCP channel; a test asserts stdout stays empty). Config failure: one ERROR line per issue then exit 1. Implement with `tracing-subscriber` JSON plus a custom formatter if needed to match field names and order. Where the log line format is asserted by a fixture, match it; the Rust engine may add OTel fields elsewhere.

# Scope boundary
This bead is dispatch, flags, usage, logging, and `migrate`. `serve` wiring, `corpus` subcommands, `mcp-stdio`, and `demo-run` bodies have their own beads; stub them here with the exact flag handling so cli.json rows for flags pass.

title: Port the provider contract: types, error taxonomy, retry policy, settings helpers, scripted test server
description:
# What
The provider contract every client implements, the exact error taxonomy, the retry policy, settings helpers, and the scripted HTTP test server. Reference Part 2 §1 and §4 (exact strings and formulas).

# Contract
- `CompletionRequest { model, system, prompt, temperature: f32, max_tokens, settings: Map<String, Value> }`; `CompletionResponse { text, tokens_in, tokens_out }`; `trait ProviderClient { async fn complete(&self, req) -> Result<CompletionResponse, ProviderError> }`.
- Temperature is f32. Clients that send it as a JSON double widen it (`0.7f32 as f64` = 0.699999988079071); Google sends float32 and prints 0.7. QUIRK Q-P1. Wire cases `*_temperature_0_7`.

# Error taxonomy (exact)
Kind: unknown, invalid_request, rate_limited, provider_error, timeout. Display: `<provider>: <kind>` + ` (status <n>)` if status != 0 + ` after <n> attempt(s)` if attempts > 0 + `: <inner>` if inner. Example: `anthropic: rate_limited (status 429) after 3 attempt(s): slow down`.
`wrap_error(provider, status, err)`, first match wins: deadline or cancel in chain -> timeout (before status); 429 -> rate_limited; >= 500 -> provider_error; >= 400 -> invalid_request (includes 408); else (0 or 1xx-3xx) -> provider_error. Retryable: rate_limited and provider_error only. A non-provider error (kind unknown) is not retryable.

# Retry (exact)
Defaults MaxAttempts 3, BaseDelay 250 ms, MaxDelay 4 s, jitter uniform [0,1). `delay(attempt)`: d = MaxDelay; shift = attempt - 1; if 0 <= shift < 32 { exp = BaseDelay << shift (i64 ns, may overflow); if 0 < exp < MaxDelay { d = exp } }; half = d / 2 (integer ns); return half + (jitter * half as f64) as i64 (truncation). Wait is in [d/2, d). `retry(ctx, policy, fn)`: sets attempts on the error; returns non-retryable or exhausted errors; on deadline during backoff returns a timeout error with the provider name and attempts (text `test: timeout after 1 attempt(s): context deadline exceeded`). Inject the jitter source and a clock so tests are deterministic. SDK-internal retries do not exist (hand-written clients).

# Settings helpers
Key `response_schema` (only Anthropic acts on it via forced tool use; OpenAI/xAI/Google ignore it). `setting_bool`, `setting_string`, `setting_int` (accepts any JSON number and truncates toward zero; strings are absent). Consumed keys: Anthropic `thinking` + `thinking_budget`; OpenAI/xAI `reasoning` -> `reasoning_effort` verbatim; Google `thinking_budget` -> `thinkingConfig.thinkingBudget`.

# Scripted test server (providertest)
An HTTP test server: records each request body; response i = script[min(i, len-1)]; optional per-response delay honoring cancellation (on cancel writes nothing); always `Content-Type: application/json`. Expose `calls()` and `last_request()`.

# D23
Clients take base URL and key only from engine config. No ambient env vars.

# Parity gate
`parity/fixtures/measurement-io/providers_core.json` (12 rows: `internal/providers/errors_test.go` 4 + `retry_test.go` 8), including `#retry_delay_default_policy_probes` (jitter 0, 0.5, 0.999999; attempts 0..7, 31..64, -1).

# Done when
All rows pass. Mutants clean on the retry math. Commit.
close_reason: Completed

The Go SDK had a 600 s per-request timeout. Keep an equivalent client timeout; the runner's per-run timeout (default 120 s) is the usual bound.

title: Port the deterministic fake provider
description:
# What
The deterministic fake provider: the only "model" allowed in CI. Used by runner tests, job tests, the API end-to-end test, demo-run, and as the judge and classifier in tests. Reference Part 2 §3 (exact validation and error strings).

# Behavior
- Fixture files: `{"fixtures":[{"model","prompt"|"prompt_sha256","output","tokens_in","tokens_out","latency_ms","error"}]}`; all but `model` optional.
- Key = `model + "\x00" + sha256hex(prompt)` (lowercase hex of exact prompt bytes). `prompt_sha256` is used verbatim, so an uppercase hash never matches (QUIRK Q-F1; reproduce).
- Add validation in order: `model is required`; `exactly one of prompt or prompt_sha256 is required` (empty string counts as absent); error in {"", rate_limited, provider_error, timeout, invalid_request} else `unknown error kind "<x>"`; duplicate -> `duplicate fixture for model "<m>" prompt hash <hash>`.
- Loading a directory: non-recursive, every `*.json` regular file in lexical order; exact error texts for read, parse, per-fixture, and "no *.json fixture files" cases.
- `complete`: lookup ignores system, temperature, max_tokens, settings. Missing -> an unknown-kind error `fake provider: no fixture for model "<model>" prompt hash <hash> (add it to testdata)`. If `latency_ms > 0`, wait that long or until the deadline (deadline -> `fake: timeout: context deadline exceeded`). Then the scripted error, or the output. With latency 0 the deadline is never consulted.
- Scripted errors: rate_limited -> status 429 `fake: rate_limited (status 429)`; provider_error -> 500; timeout -> `fake: timeout: context deadline exceeded`; invalid_request -> 400. The fake never retries.
- Use tokio time so tests can pause and advance time.

# Parity gate
`parity/fixtures/measurement-io/fake_provider.json` (9 rows, `internal/providers/fake/fake_test.go`).

# Done when
All rows pass. Commit.

title: Port byte-identical prompt assembly (PromptText, Assemble)
description:
# What
Byte-identical prompt assembly for benchmark runs: the same bytes for every column, so differences in results come from the model, not the prompt. Reference Part 2 §5.1.

# PromptText(task)
- attachments = [] if task.attachments is empty bytes; else JSON-decode (error -> `parsing attachments: <err>`; JSON null -> empty; element fields `name`, `content`; unknown fields ignored; Go's case-insensitive field matching applies, so `Name` also matches; serde needs aliases or a custom decoder).
- out = task.prompt; for each attachment in order: `out += "\n\n--- attachment: " + name + " ---\n" + content`. No trimming, no trailing newline; empty name/content still emits the header.

# Assemble(task, column)
1. PromptText error -> `task <task.id>: <err>`.
2. Settings: empty bytes -> none; else decode into a map (numbers become f64); error -> `column <column.id>: parsing settings: <err>`; JSON null or {} -> none; a JSON array is an error.
3. Returns `{model: column.model_id, system: "", prompt, temperature: task.temperature (f32), max_tokens, settings}`. The system slot is ALWAYS empty for benchmark runs.
Error text after the prefixes embeds Go JSON library text. D36 (owner-decided): keep the engine-authored prefixes (`task <id>: parsing attachments: `, `column <id>: parsing settings: `) byte for byte; the library tail is Rust's own text and is not compared. Tag such assertions D36.

# Parity gate
`internal/runner/assemble_test.go` (5 manifest rows), goldens `testdata/internal/runner/testdata/assemble_*.golden` (the basic golden is exactly the prompt, 69 bytes, no newline).

# Done when
All rows pass byte for byte. Commit.

title: Port the benchmark runner: worker pools, pacer, statuses, cost, run persistence, resume hook
description:
# What
The benchmark runner: executes a batch of (task x column x repeats), per-provider worker pools bounded by concurrency and requests per minute, sequential repeats, per-run timeout, status taxonomy, cost from the price snapshot, and one `runs` row per repeat. Reference Part 2 §5.2 to §5.7 (exact algorithm, texts, and the test catalog).

# Key rules
- Config: repeats (batch value if > 0, else `MAVERICK_RUNNER_REPEATS`, default 3); per-run timeout default 120 s (max 600 s); per provider `MAX_CONCURRENCY` default 8 and `RPM_LIMIT` default 0 (unthrottled).
- Skip columns whose status is not cold_start, active, or deprecated (log `skipping non-runnable column`); retired columns write no rows.
- Providers run concurrently; per provider, workers = min(max_concurrency, pairs); FIFO of pairs; one pacer per provider per run.
- All repeats of a pair run sequentially on one worker (repeats measure variance, not throughput).
- Setup error precedence and texts: attachments, settings, pricing (`parsing pricing snapshot: ...`, `pricing snapshot has a negative price`), client (`no provider client configured for "<provider>" (column <id>)`). A setup error writes a provider_error row per repeat with no latency and zero cost.
- execute: latency (ms, truncated) is set on EVERY executed row, success or failure. timeout if kind timeout or deadline in chain; else provider_error (rate limits, 5xx after retries, invalid request, unknown errors like a missing fake fixture). Success: status ok, output (even empty), tokens always set. The runner never writes parse_failure.
- Cost = round((in * p_in + out * p_out) / 1e6 * 1e6) / 1e6 with round half AWAY from zero (Go `math.Round`; Rust `f64::round` matches). Persist as decimal text with 6 places into `numeric(12,6)`. Summary cost = f64 sum of rounded per-run costs in completion order.
- Pacer: interval = 60 s / rpm in integer ns; first call claims now; each later start one interval after the previous claimed slot; a cancelled context fails even with no wait; a claimed slot is not given back.
- Persistence: one `InsertRun` per repeat immediately after it finishes (no batching, no transaction). Persistence failures are collected (`persisting run <id> (<task> x <column> repeat <n>): <err>`) and returned joined; provider failures never produce a returned error.
- Log `batch complete` with batch_id, runs_total, runs_ok, runs_error, spend_usd, duration_ms.

# Rust additions for the jobs package (D10)
The batch id comes from the caller (the deterministic batches id), not a fresh ULID, when the jobs package runs a batch. Support resume: skip (column, task, repeat) triples that already have a `runs` row for this batch id. Provide this as an input set of done triples, or a query hook, so the Go-parity tests still see Go behavior when the set is empty.

# Parity gate
`parity/fixtures/measurement-io/runner.json` (9 rows) and `internal/runner/runner_test.go` (10 tests: taxonomy, skip retired, setup failure, concurrency bound and sequential repeats, pacer spacing, rpm limit, two Postgres batch tests, cost numeric round trip). Use tokio paused time for timing tests where possible so CI is not flaky.

# Done when
All rows pass. Commit.

title: Write the opt-in, spend-capped live smoke test (no keys needed to write it)
description:
# What
WRITE the one opt-in, spend-capped live smoke test: the ONLY test allowed to call real providers. Reference Part 2 §14; spec §15; master plan §6. RUNNING it with real keys is a separate, final-stage bead that depends on the owner's keys; this bead needs no keys and blocks nothing on the owner.

# Behavior (port exactly)
- Gate: skip unless `MAVERICK_LIVE_SMOKE == "1"` (skip text begins `live smoke is opt-in and spend-capped (spec §15)`). Also mark the test `#[ignore]` so `cargo test` never runs it by accident.
- Columns: default `anthropic/claude-haiku-4-5` (1.00/5.00 USD per Mtok) and `openai/gpt-5.4-mini` (0.60/2.40), or `MAVERICK_LIVE_SMOKE_COLUMNS` = exactly 2 entries `provider:model_id:input_per_mtok:output_per_mtok`. Column id `livesmoke-<provider>-<model>`, endpoint direct, settings {}, active, pricing JSON with source `livesmoke`.
- Keys from `MAVERICK_{ANTHROPIC,OPENAI,GOOGLE,XAI}_API_KEY`; missing -> skip, listing the missing names (never the values).
- Two synthetic tasks with exact prompts from the reference: `live-smoke-extraction`, `live-smoke-summarization`. They are not corpus tasks.
- Spend: projected spend (repeats 1) must be <= $1.00 before any call; accumulate actual cost; fatal once >= $1.00.
- For each column and task: assemble, complete under 90 s, assert non-blank text, tokens_in > 0, tokens_out > 0, latency > 0. Never assert scores.
- Detailed logging: one structured line per call with provider, model, task id, status, latency_ms, tokens, cost, running total. Never log prompt text, output text, or keys.
- A `make live-smoke` equivalent (script or cargo alias).

# Verify without keys
Run the test against the scripted HTTP test server (point base URLs at it through engine config) to prove the flow, the spend math, and the logging, with fake keys. CI still never runs the real gate.

# Done when
The test exists, skips by default, and passes against the scripted server with fake keys. Commit.

title: Build the axum server skeleton: routers, middleware chain, wire encoding, strict decoding, error envelope
description:
# What
The axum server skeleton for both listeners: routers, the 404/405 behavior, the middleware chain, the exact JSON wire encoding, strict request decoding, and the error envelope with the full error catalog. Reference Part 5 §1 to §5 (exact); spec Appendix A and B.

# Routing (reference Part 5 §1)
Two independent routers. No redirects, no trailing-slash normalization, no HEAD-from-GET, no OPTIONS/CORS. Public `:8080`: `GET /up` (no auth), `any /mcp`, `/v1/config/{pools,weights,constraints}` GET/PUT, `GET /v1/policies`, `POST /v1/recommend`, `GET /v1/checks/*` (wildcard keeps slashes), `GET /v1/models`, `POST /v1/telemetry`, `/v1/history/*`, `/v1/debug/*`. Internal `:8081`: `GET /health/detail`, `/internal/v1/*` (Part 5 §1.2 table). Unmatched and wrong-method requests reach the 404 handler after RequestID, Logger, Recoverer (check the reference for whether wrong method is 404 or 405 in Go; chi returned 405 in some cases; the fixture `x_method_not_allowed` style rows and the replay decide).

# Middleware order (outermost first, both listeners)
1. RequestID: read `X-Request-ID`; if empty or > 128 bytes mint a ULID (26 chars, uppercase Crockford, monotonic); set the response header BEFORE the handler so every response (401/404/429/500) carries it.
2. Logger: one line per request (see the logging bead).
3. Recoverer: on panic log `panic recovered` with request_id, panic, stack; if nothing was written yet, write 500 `internal_error` / `internal error`.
4. Route match.
5. Public `/v1` and `/mcp`: Auth, then RateLimit, then BodyLimit (2 MiB = 2097152 bytes). Internal: InternalAuth for everything, then BodyLimit only under `/internal/v1`.
Consequences pinned by tests: an unauthenticated request never touches the limiter; a rate-limited request never has its body read; an oversize body with a valid key is counted by the limiter first, so the 413 carries `X-RateLimit-*`; 401/403 carry `X-Request-ID` but no rate-limit headers. Chunked (unknown length) oversize bodies must also 413 (`TestConfigOversizeBodyChunked413`).

# Wire encoding (Part 5 §3) and decoding (§4)
Every JSON body ends with exactly one `\n` (Go `json.Encoder`). Match Go's escaping (Go escapes `<`, `>`, `&` as `<` etc. by default; check the reference) and number formatting. Strict decoding: unknown fields rejected, trailing data rejected, as Go did. D25: `malformed request body:` prefix, status, and code match; the detail after the prefix is Rust's own text (tag D25).

# Error envelope and catalog (Part 5 §5)
`{"error":{"code","message","details":{}}}` exact, with every template the API writes (§5.2). Rust adds `409 no_compliant_columns` and `422 zero_retention_requires_declared`.

# Parity gate
`parity/fixtures/api/apierrors.json` (4 rows), `middleware.json` (18 rows incl. rate limiter unit cases), `error_catalog_observed.json`, and `server_test.go` routing/body-cap rows (22 tests; auth and rate-limit rows are shared with the auth bead).

# Done when
Rows pass. Commit.
close_reason: Implemented axum routers, wire errors, request IDs, panic recovery, strict JSON helpers, and body limits; focused tests pass.

title: Implement the internal provisioning seam (tenants, keys, config, alerts, columns, limits, corpus activate)
description:
# What
The internal provisioning API, "the Rails seam", built before Rails exists. Internal listener only. Reference Part 5 §7 and §13.12; spec §13; master plan §3.3.

# Endpoints
- `POST /internal/v1/tenants` `{name}`: one transaction: create tenant (32-byte HMAC key minted, status active) and, only if at least one active column exists, a default pool of all active columns (`is_default = true`). The active-column list is read before BEGIN. A new tenant arrives usable.
- `GET /internal/v1/tenants/{id}`: tenant + config summary.
- `POST /internal/v1/tenants/{id}/suspend` and `/activate`.
- `POST /internal/v1/tenants/{id}/api-keys` `{name}` -> `{id, key}`; raw key returned once.
- `DELETE /internal/v1/api-keys/{id}`: revoke.
- `PUT /internal/v1/tenants/{id}/{pools|weights|constraints}`: same payloads and SAME G4 validation code as `/v1/config/*`.
- `GET /internal/v1/alerts?since=&kind=`: operator alert feed.
- `POST /internal/v1/columns`, `PUT /internal/v1/columns/{id}`: catalog administration; retirement guard (blocks and alerts); retention rules (valid_until <= verified_at + 90 days else 422 invalid_request; a retention downgrade runs the G4 simulation and raises a critical alert per affected zero-retention tenant but is not blocked); endpoint values `direct|vertex|bedrock|azure|openrouter` enforced here (no DB CHECK); `execution_aliases` with per-alias retention (D15).
- NEW: `PUT /internal/v1/tenants/{id}/limits` `{classification_daily_quota?}` (null clears; response echoes effective values) (D4).
- `POST /internal/v1/corpus/activate`.
All writes append a structured audit log entry naming the actor label (`audit=true`); catalog changes log their own lines (Part 5 §10.2, §10.3).

# Rules
Internal callers are root (no tenant scoping). The engine never calls Rails (G9).

# Parity gate
`internalv1_test.go` (18 tests), replay rows. New tests for the limits endpoint and retention validation.

# Done when
Rows pass. Commit.
close_reason: Completed: /internal/v1 seam (tenants, keys, config, limits D4, alerts, columns with guard + retention D1/D15, corpus activate); 18 internalv1 rows + UnknownPaths tagged; byte-exact error bodies from recordings

title: Implement operator capture reads on the internal listener
description:
# What
Operator (internal, audited) capture reads: `GET /internal/v1/captures` and `GET /internal/v1/captures/{id}/prompt`. Reference Part 4 §4.6 ("ReadPrompt (internal, root)") and Part 5 §7.11, §7.12, §13.11.

# Rules
- Root access: unscoped lookup across tenants.
- On miss: find any `delete` row in the access log; none -> log `read` with tenant "" and return 404; found -> log `read` with that row's tenant and return 410 `capture_expired`.
- Shared tail with the tenant read: expired -> log `read` with the capture's tenant -> 410; else decrypt (by `capture_key_version`, D18), load the recommendation, log `read` (actor = operator label), return `{id, tenant_id, prompt, prompt_hash, recommendation_id, classification, captured_at, expires_at}`.
- Every read lands in `capture_access_log`, which outlives the capture.
- The prompt is returned in the response body only. It must never appear in a log line, span, or metric (G5).

# Parity gate
`internalv1_captures_test.go` (10 tests), replay rows.

Rows pass. Commit.

title: Implement /up and /health/detail (job_queue component from graphile_worker, D35)
description:
# What
`GET /up` (public, no auth) and `GET /health/detail` (internal, token). Reference Part 5 §8 (Go bodies); spec §9.9; `docs/api.md` "GET /health/detail"; `parity/DIVERGENCES.md` D35 (owner decision 2026-09-28). `/up` is the Kamal health check.

# /up
Ping the DB with a 2 s timeout. 200 `{"status":"ok"}`; failure 503 `{"status":"unavailable"}`. GET only.

# /health/detail
- Ping failure: `degraded`, 503, `components.db = {"status":"error","detail":"<driver error text>"}` (driver text is a library tail, D36), `components.job_queue = {"status":"unknown","detail":"database unreachable"}`, `active_matrix_version: null`, `last_batch_times: null`.
- Success: `db {"status":"ok"}`; `active_matrix_version` = active corpus version or null; queue read failure -> `job_queue {"status":"unknown","detail":"querying job queue state failed"}` and `last_batch_times: null`, overall still ok/200; success -> the `job_queue` component and `last_batch_times` (`{}` when none).
- `provider_client_config`: providers in order anthropic, openai, google, xai with non-empty keys; none -> `none_configured` / `no provider API keys set`; else `ok` / `configured: anthropic, openai`.
- Body keys: `status`, `components` (sorted: `db`, `job_queue`, `provider_client_config`), `active_matrix_version`, `last_batch_times`. Component `detail` is omitted when empty.

# job_queue component (D35)
Fed from graphile_worker state (store bead 3.6). Rules: no registered worker -> `no_workers`; no worker heartbeat newer than 60 s -> `stale` (detail names the seconds and queues); else `ok` (detail `graphile_worker queues: <names>`). There is no `paused` status. `last_batch_times` maps job kind to the latest `batches.completed_at` (graphile_worker deletes completed jobs, so the `batches` table is the source). An `--api-only` node reports the workers of a separate `--worker-only` node, because the state lives in Postgres.

# Parity gate
`health_internal_test.go` (1), `server_test.go` /up rows (incl. `TestUpReturns503WhenDatabaseUnreachable`), `parity/fixtures/api/health_river_queues.json` (5 rows: restate each case for `job_queue`; the `paused` case becomes a D35-tagged row with no Rust equivalent), replay rows (tag D35 where the body differs).

# Tests (detailed logging)
Worker registered and fresh -> ok; no worker -> no_workers; stale heartbeat -> stale; DB down -> 503 degraded; last_batch_times from seeded `batches` rows. On failure print the full JSON body.

# Done when
Rows pass. Commit.
close_reason: Completed: maverick_api::health. GET /up pings with a 2 s timeout: 200 {"status":"ok"}\n, else 503 {"status":"unavailable"}\n; GET only. GET /health/detail (internal token): Go body keys/order/escaping + trailing newline; ping failure -> 503 degraded, db error with driver text, job_queue unknown 'database unreachable', nulls; success -> db ok, active_matrix_version or null, job_queue from graphile_worker._private_workers (D35: no_workers 'no graphile_worker worker is registered' / stale 'no worker heartbeat for Ns (graphile_worker queues: default)' when freshest > 60 s / ok 'graphile_worker queues: default'; no paused), last_batch_times from batches.completed_at (Go time JSON); queue read failure -> unknown 'querying job queue state failed', last_batch_times null, still 200; provider_client_config from config keys. Router: public_router_with / internal_router_with take a HealthState; old builders use HealthState::detached(). 11 api rows tagged (TestRiverQueuesComponent + 5 subtests restated for D35, TestUpOK, TestUp503, 3 internal health rows); 7 unit + 8 DB tests pass. The no_workers and stale detail wordings are my D35 choice (docs/api.md fixes only the ok example).
