title: Implement the batches lease: claim, no-op outcomes, takeover, heartbeat, deterministic id (D10)
description:
# What
The engine-owned `batches` lease that gives every job per-(kind, window) uniqueness (D10). This replaces River's unique jobs, because graphile_worker deletes completed jobs, so its `job_key` cannot stop a re-enqueue after completion from running a second time. Spec §11.2; master plan §3.1.

# Claim (first transaction of every handler)
Insert the `batches` row for (kind, batch_window) if absent: deterministic `id`, `status = running`, `lease_owner` = the graphile_worker worker id, `lease_expires_at`, `heartbeat_at`, `attempt = 1`. Or take it over if its lease expired. Outcomes:
- `completed` or `skipped` row -> the handler is a no-op and returns success.
- Live lease held by a different worker that is still alive -> return success as a no-op. NEVER fail (a failure would burn `max_attempts` into a permanent failure). Nothing is stranded: the holder's own job stays locked, and graphile recovers it if the holder dies.
- Owner gone (graphile recovered the job from that worker) -> take over IMMEDIATELY, even before `lease_expires_at`. Determining "owner is gone" needs graphile_worker's worker/lock state; read how 0.13.x records locked_by and recovery, and base the rule on that.
- Stale running row -> take over; `attempt` increments; the batch resumes under the SAME id from its existing `runs`.

# Heartbeat
The holder renews `lease_expires_at` and `heartbeat_at` well inside the expiry (for example every TTL/3). If a renew finds the lease lost, stop work promptly.

# Resume and idempotency
Delivery is at-least-once, so every handler is idempotent: a batch resumes by skipping (column, task, repeat) triples that already have a `runs` row for this id (the runner's resume hook); the rebuild is keyed by batch. A spend refusal records the window as `skipped`.

# Deterministic id
`bat_` + a deterministic ULID-shaped value from (kind, window) (for example a hash-derived 128-bit value), equal to `runs.batch_id` for batch kinds. Document the derivation; it must be stable across processes and releases.

# Tests (real Postgres)
Concurrent claimers: exactly one runs. Completed -> no-op. Live foreign lease -> no-op success. Expired lease -> takeover with attempt 2 and same id. Heartbeat renewal. Lease-lost detection.

# Done when
Tests pass. Commit.
close_reason: Completed

title: Wire the G8 spend guard into batches (window actuals, refusal -> skipped, 80% warning)
description:
# What
The G8 spend guard as it runs inside batch jobs: projection plus window actuals against the nightly and weekly caps, refusal and warning alerts, and the skipped batch. Reference Part 3 §2.6 (exact formulas, subject keys, message formats) and §6 spend guard tests; spec §11.

# Rules
- Projection from the domain bead (`ProjectSpend`): runes not bytes; `est_in = (runes + 3) / 4 + 600`; per_run = (est_in * in_price + max_tokens * out_price) / 1e6; x repeats; pricing error text `jobs: projecting spend: column %s: %w`.
- Windows over `runs.ran_at` (half-open): nightStart = night 00:00 UTC, nightEnd = +1 day, weekStart = nightStart - 6 days. `nightTotal = nightSpent + projected`, `weekTotal = weekSpent + projected`.
- Refuse iff `(applyNightly && nightTotal > nightlyCap) || weekTotal > weeklyCap` (strict). applyNightly is false for weekly_sweep. Insert `spend_refusal` critical; the batch does not run; record the window as `skipped` (D10).
- Else warn iff `(applyNightly && nightTotal >= 0.8 * nightlyCap) || weekTotal >= 0.8 * weeklyCap`: `spend_warning` warning; run. QUIRK J7: cap 0 with a zero projection fires a warning.
- Subject keys: `job, night, nightly_cap_usd, night_spent_usd, planned_runs, projected_usd, weekly_cap_usd, week_spent_usd`. Messages exact (reference; `spend.json#messages`), including `(≥80%)`.
- A failed alert insert returns `jobs: writing %s alert: %w` and the job retries.
- Actual spend accumulates per batch so projections are auditable (batch output `projected_usd`, `actual_usd`).
- Duplicate provider calls after a crash (between a successful call and its runs commit) are bounded by this accounting.

# Parity gate
`parity/fixtures/measurement-core/spend.json` (2 rows) and the five DB tests: refuses over nightly cap, refuses over weekly cap, warns at 80%, allows under cap, sums window actuals.

# Done when
Rows pass. Commit.
close_reason: Completed: G8 spend guard for batches (window actuals, refusal, 80% warning, J7); five Go DB tests pass

title: Implement nightly_smoke and weekly_sweep: composition, resume, grading pass, transactional failure tail (D11)
description:
# What
The `nightly_smoke` and `weekly_sweep` handlers: batch composition, the prediction-lock precondition, the spend guard, execution through the runner with resume, the grading pass, completion accounting, and the failure tail written in the same transaction as the batch outcome (D11). Reference Part 3 §2.4, §2.5, §2.7; spec §11; master plan §3.1.

# Composition
- nightly_smoke: tasks = active tasks of the active corpus (by id); columns = runnable (cold_start, active, deprecated; by id). Groups: (smoke-member tasks x non-cold columns) then (ALL tasks x cold_start columns). Both caps apply.
- weekly_sweep: (all tasks x all runnable columns), weekly cap only, full-length long-context tasks.
- repeats = `MAVERICK_RUNNER_REPEATS` (3 if <= 0).

# Steps
1. Claim the `batches` lease (lease bead). No-op outcomes return success.
2. Project spend over groups (error -> job error/retry). Zero planned runs -> log `batch has nothing to run`, output `{completion_pct: 1}`, mark the window completed, no rebuild.
3. Lock precondition: count predictions for the night; zero -> warn `no predictions locked for tonight; batch proceeds unscored (spec 11 prediction_lock)`, `lock_missing: true`, continue.
4. Spend guard: refused -> `refused: true`, window `skipped`, no runs, no rebuild.
5. batch_id = the deterministic `batches.id` (D10; Go minted a fresh `bat_` ULID per execution). Run each group through the runner with resume (skip triples already in `runs`). Runner persistence errors are logged, not returned. Heartbeat the lease throughout.
6. List runs by batch; grade every run with output (grading pass below).
7. completed_runs = runs with status ok or parse_failure; completion_pct = completed / planned.
8. Failure tail + outcome in ONE transaction (D11): mark the batch `completed`, write `job_failure` warning if completion_pct < 0.9 (strict; message `%s %s completed %d/%d runs (%.1f%%)`), write `job_failure` warning if judge failures / attempts >= 0.1 (message in the reference, threshold printed as 10), and enqueue `aggregate_rebuild {night, batch_id}` using graphile_worker's SQL `add_job` inside the same transaction. No detached tasks carry durable work. Alert fan-out (email/webhook) happens after commit and never blocks.
9. Return success once runs exist (never retried after that), with the batch output `{batch_id?, refused?, lock_missing?, spend_warned?, projected_usd, actual_usd, planned_runs, completed_runs, completion_pct, graded_runs, judge_attempts?, judge_failures?}`.

# Grading pass (reference §2.7)
For each run with output (order task_id, column, repeat): find the task (unknown -> log, skip); decode grader specs (fail -> log, skip); per envelope: parse; judge -> count attempt; grade (error -> judge failure if judge, warn, skip; dimensions absent); map dimensions; empty -> skip; `SaveScores(run, idx, mapped, detail)`. A run with any saved grader counts as graded. On resume, do not re-grade runs that already have scores (idempotency); check the reference for Go's behavior and document the Rust rule.

# Go quirks to review
J3 (expired context makes completion 0%) and J9 (SIGTERM cancels running jobs and the partial batch completes and is never retried). With the lease and resume, the Rust behavior improves on both; these changes fall under D10/D11. Record them in the tests with D10/D11 tags.

# Parity gate
Reference Part 3 §6 batch tests (TestFinishBatch* restated for the transactional tail), `parity/manifest/measurement-core.json` jobs rows. Sunday: both batches for the same night, two rebuilds with distinct batch ids.

# Done when
Rows pass. Commit.

title: Implement aggregate_rebuild (bit-exact f32 fold, D6 availability, D7 censored latency, chained enqueue)
description:
# What
`aggregate_rebuild`: the choke point that turns a batch's runs and scores into folded cell aggregates. Reference Part 3 §2.9; spec §6.1 to §6.4.

# Steps (exact order)
1. Claim the lease for (aggregate_rebuild, batch_id) (keyed by batch).
2. runs = list by batch. None -> log, zero output, success (still chains).
3. scores = list by batch ordered (run_id, grader_idx, dimension), grouped per run into grader entries {idx, dims widened from f32, detail from the grader's first row}.
4. Per run: load the task (cached; error -> job error); run quality with dimension weights (error -> `task %s dimension_weights: %w`), the overlay for high-stakes, f32 pass threshold, autofail over each grader's detail.
5. Cell = (column, capability, tier); the cell's matrix_version is from the first run seen. Append run stats (pass, latency if non-null, cost if decodable).
6. Per (task, column) pair: collect gradable q and shared-dimension spreads.
7. Cells sorted by (column, capability, tier); pairs by (task, column). Task outcome = ambiguity penalty(variance penalty(q).score, ambiguity(spreads)); gradable = at least one q.
8. Fold observations with AsOf = night, matrix_version, alpha, min_nights. Re-folding a night is idempotent (the same night replaces, n does not double count).
9. On success enqueue `regression_scan` then `calibration_score` with {night, batch_id}. Go used the job context for this (QUIRK J12) and wrote a critical `job_failure` alert per failed enqueue (message `aggregate_rebuild %s could not enqueue %s for batch %s: %v`). In Rust, enqueue them in the same transaction as the completion (D11) so they cannot be lost.

# Divergences
D6: add the `availability` dimension (fraction of scheduled repeats that returned output, errors and timeouts included in the denominator) and exclude error runs from quality. D7: latency percentiles include timeouts censored at the timeout value (the timeout is the runner's per-run timeout). Tag tests.

# Parity gate
Bit-exact float32 fixtures: `ewma.json#fold_observations_via_float32_storage/*`, `observe.json`; DB tests TestFoldObservationsThreeNights (values within 1e-5 and bit-exact f32), TestFoldObservationsMultipleDimensions, TestSaveScoresRoundTrip; the property tests (run quality bounds, penalty properties, shared-dimension spread bounds, variance sigma formula within 1e-12, EWMA bounds, resume matches direct fold).

# Done when
Rows pass bit-exact where required. Commit.
close_reason: Completed: aggregate_rebuild (bit-exact f32 fold, D6, D7, D11 chained enqueue), FoldObservations/SaveScores, scoring properties; Postgres tests pass

title: Implement regression_scan with dedup, severity by tenant bar, and the parse-failure watch
description:
# What
`regression_scan` with the parse-failure watch. Reference Part 3 §2.10; spec §6.5, §11; domain math from the regression bead.

# Steps
1. Cells = every `quality` aggregate row with `as_of = night` (ALL cells folded that night, not only this batch's; QUIRK J4, so on Sundays the second scan is a no-op through dedup).
2. Per cell: series = quality rows with as_of <= night (widened f32); detect regressions; keep findings with AsOf == night.
3. Dedup state: existing `regression` alerts for the cell (subject match on model_column_id, capability, difficulty_tier compared as TEXT), ordered (created_at, id); state = latest as_of (ties keep the earlier row). Filter: alert again only after 7 days or if 2 points deeper.
4. Severity: pools containing the column (ordered tenant_id, name), each tenant once; bar = tenant_weights.quality_bar for the capability (widened f32) else 0.80; critical if the drop crosses any tenant's bar, else warning.
5. Alert subject keys: `as_of, baseline, batch_id, capability, current, delta, difficulty_tier, dimension, model_column_id, regression_kind` (`drop` | `shock`). The first five are the history-marker contract. Message exact with U+2192 arrow and U+2212 minus: `quality regression (%s) on %s %s tier %d: %.1f → %.1f (−%.1f pts) as of %s`.

# Parse-failure watch
Batch rate per column (runs of this batch), trailing rate over runs with ran_at in [nightStart - 7 days, nightStart) (QUIRK J5: wall clock), already-alerted columns for this night. Alert iff rate > 0.05 AND rate > 2.0 x trailing (both strict). Kind `parse_failure_rate`, warning, subject keys `batch_id, model_column_id, night, parse_failure_rate, parse_failures, total_runs, trailing_rate`, message exact with U+00D7.

# Output
`{batch_id, cells_scanned, regression_alerts, parse_failure_alerts}`. Claim the lease keyed by batch; re-running a night is a no-op.

# Parity gate
`regression.json` (DB-backed cases) and reference Part 3 §6 regression_scan tests.

# Done when
Rows pass. Commit.
close_reason: Completed

title: Implement prediction_lock and calibration_score
description:
# What
`prediction_lock` (02:50) and `calibration_score` (chained after rebuild). Reference Part 3 §2.8, §2.11, §3; master plan §3.1 "Calibration".

# prediction_lock
1. Active corpus, active tasks, runnable columns.
2. Scheduled cells = {(column, capability, tier)} for smoke x non-cold plus all x cold_start; if `cronFiresOn(MAVERICK_CRON_WEEKLY, night)` also all x all runnable (`sweep_night: true`).
3. Latest `pass_rate` aggregate per cell (any date; QUIRK J11: if tonight's rebuild already exists, that row is used).
4. Derive: cells without an EWMA are skipped; p = clamp(ewma, 0, 1); sorted by (column, capability, tier); each once.
5. Insert with `batch_id = the NIGHT tag` (not a runner batch id), `predicted_pass_prob = f32(p)`, `source = "ewma"`, `matrix_version = active corpus`, `locked_at = now`; ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING (first lock wins).
Output `{night, sweep_night, scheduled_cells, locked_cells, inserted_rows}`.
Why: locking before results makes hindsight impossible; the `source` column lets later predictors (matrix completion, IRT) compete on the same ledger.

# calibration_score
1. Locked predictions for the night tag; none -> warn, `skipped: true`.
2. Runs of the batch; none -> skipped.
3. Per run: run quality (same choke point as rebuild); p = locked prob for its cell; missing -> `unlocked_runs++`; else append {p, pass} under the capability.
4. Per capability (sorted): upsert calibration (batch_id = the REAL batch id, capability, brier f32, overconfidence f32, n); conflict updates values and scored_at.
Output `{batch_id, locked_cells, pairs, unlocked_runs, calibration_rows, skipped?}`.

# Parity gate
`predictions.json` DB-backed cases and reference Part 3 §6 predictions and jobs tests. Lease-claim both handlers (prediction_lock by night; calibration by batch).

# Done when
Rows pass. Commit.
close_reason: Completed

title: Implement latency_probes for secondary-endpoint columns
description:
# What
`latency_probes` (hourly): thin pings for secondary-endpoint columns, feeding their latency cells only. Reference Part 3 §2.12; spec §11; master plan §3.1 ("quality is a property of the model, latency and price are properties of the path to it").

# Rules (exact)
- Probe prompt: the 60-character string `Reply with the single word pong to this latency probe line. ` (trailing space) repeated 67 times (4020 chars). max_tokens 100, temperature 0, settings = column settings (none when empty). 5 sequential pings per column.
- Columns: runnable (by id) with `quality_source_column_id` set. Source cells = latest `quality` and `pass_rate` aggregates of the SOURCE column, one per (capability, tier), first row in query order (pass_rate sorts first, so its matrix_version wins). No measured check (QUIRK J6). No source cells -> skip without probing.
- Missing client or bad settings -> 5 failures, no pings. Each ping timeout = `MAVERICK_RUNNER_TIMEOUT`. Latency = elapsed ms (truncated) of successful calls. A cancelled job stops early without counting remaining pings.
- At least one success: `{latency_p50_ms, latency_p95_ms}` by nearest rank over sorted successes; fold into each source cell ON THE PROBE COLUMN with AsOf = UTC date of the `hour` arg and the source row's matrix_version. Later passes on the same day replace the day's row (n increments once per day).
- Output `{columns, probes_ok, probes_failed, cells_updated}`.
- These calls use operator keys (benchmark use); in CI only the fake provider.

# Parity gate
Reference Part 3 §6 latency_probes tests.

# Done when
Rows pass. Commit.
close_reason: Completed: latency_probes (source cells, 5 pings, p50/p95 fold on the probe column, same-day replace); Postgres tests pass

title: Implement price_sync and catalog_sync (lifecycle, retirement guard, drift check, retention_expiring)
description:
# What
`price_sync` (06:00) and `catalog_sync` (06:10). Reference Part 3 §2.13 and §5; spec §4.1 to §4.5, §7.2, §11.

# price_sync
1. No price source configured -> info log, zero output (Go behavior; still valid). Define the price-source trait here; the models.dev implementation (owner decision 2026-09-28) is bead 7.15.
2. Source error -> job error.
3. Per runnable column (by id): look up (provider, model_id, endpoint); missing -> count; equal input/output/currency -> skip (as_of and source not compared); else snapshot JSON `{"input_per_mtok","output_per_mtok","currency","as_of","source"}` (as_of defaults to the job day), update the column preserving every other field, log `catalog_changes` change=pricing. Historical `runs.cost` is NEVER restated.
Output `{columns, updated, missing_from_source}`.

# catalog_sync
1. measured = columns with any `measured = true` aggregate.
2. cold_start columns: activate when `cold_start_until` is set, day >= it, and measured.
3. deprecated columns: when `deprecation_date` <= day, run the retirement guard; blocked -> count and warn (the guard already wrote the critical alert; QUIRK J8: it re-alerts every day); allowed -> `retired`.
4. Drift check: every pool whose G4 survivors <= 1 -> `pool_would_be_empty`, critical at 0 (`has no usable columns`), warning at 1 (`is within one column of empty`); subject keys and message exact (Go `%q` quoting of the pool name). No dedup (J8). The drift simulation includes zero retention (D1).
5. NEW (spec §4.5): `retention_expiring` warning 14 days before any column's or alias's `retention_valid_until`. Expired evidence reads as `unknown` everywhere, which can empty a zero-retention pool; the drift check must catch it.
6. Status changes log `catalog_changes` change=status.
Output `{activated, retired, retirement_blocked, drift_alerts}` plus a retention counter.

# Parity gate
`catalog.json` DB-backed cases and reference Part 3 §6 catalog tests; new retention tests.

# Done when
Rows pass. Commit.
close_reason: Completed: price_sync (PriceSource trait, StaticPrices, Go snapshot JSON), catalog_sync (lifecycle, retirement guard, drift check incl. D1, retention_expiring), Go-exact pool_floor in the domain, store simulation state loader; 5 Go rows tagged; mutants 0 missed

title: Build the sdk-conformance mock engine and mock provider servers with a language-neutral control API
description:
# What
The `sdk-conformance` crate's servers: a mock MM engine and a mock provider that run scripted scenarios, as a binary that SDK repos (TypeScript, Ruby, Go, Python) start in their CI. `plans/model-maverick-sdk-v0-plan.md` §2.3; master plan §3.5, §7.2 N2.

# Mock engine
- `POST /v1/recommend`: scripted responses per scenario (declared and prompt forms; chains with `settings`, `retention_mode`, `execution_aliases`; `zero_retention` flag; the terminal errors `422 zero_retention_requires_declared` and `409 no_compliant_columns`; outage by refusing connections or 5xx).
- `POST /v1/telemetry`: records every batch byte for byte so scenarios can assert shape, timing, and "zero bytes when off".
- Records every recommend request (form, projection version, headers) for assertions.

# Mock provider
Scripted per scenario: 2xx, 429 with `Retry-After`, 500, timeout (slow headers), connection refused, 400/422 semantic errors, SSE streams. Speaks the OpenAI chat-completions and Anthropic Messages shapes, plus an OpenRouter-like endpoint for the openrouter mode.

# Control interface
A small control API or CLI (`sdk-conformance serve --scenario <name>` or a control endpoint to load a scenario and read results) so a test in any language can drive it. Keep it language-neutral: HTTP + JSON only. Document it in the crate README.

# Rules
No provider schema translation anywhere. No real network. Deterministic.

# Done when
Both mock servers run from the binary and a Rust smoke test drives one scenario through them. Commit.

title: Freeze the conformance scenarios and JSON test vectors (incl. zero-retention and OpenRouter cases)
description:
# What
The frozen cross-language scenarios and JSON test vectors. sdk-v0 plan §2.3 ("twelve frozen scenarios"; the plan enumerates nine numbered groups, some with sub-cases; freeze the list with stable ids and record the mapping); openrouter spec (conformance additions); master plan §3.5, §3.6.

# Scenarios (enumerated once, frozen as the contract)
1. Declared-form happy path; prompt-form happy path.
2. Provider 429 with `Retry-After` -> chain advances after the wait.
3. Provider 500 / timeout / connection refused -> chain advances.
4. Provider 400/422 -> no advance, error surfaced verbatim.
5. Chain exhausted -> last provider error surfaced.
6. MM down -> cached chain used; cold cache -> default model; `privacy: off` -> MM never contacted. Zero-retention: (a) engine answers 422 `zero_retention_requires_declared` or 409 `no_compliant_columns` -> error surfaced, no fail-open, cached chains for the tenant purged; (b) warm-cache outage for a ZR tenant -> only `zero`-stamped entries used; (c) cold-cache outage for a ZR tenant -> fail closed unless the default model is locally marked verified zero-retention.
7. Telemetry: batch shape, interval flush, exit flush, silent drop on failure; `check_pass` absent when no check ran (never defaulted to true); `settings_applied` set when entry settings were applied.
8. `MODELMAVERICK_TELEMETRY=off` -> zero bytes to `/v1/telemetry` (asserted by the mock).
9. Alias parsing table, including pass-through of concrete model names and the `?settings=caller` suffix (entry settings applied by default, left alone with the suffix). The prompt-form request carries the workload projection and its version; an `X-Maverick-Workload` override sends the declared form.
Plus (openrouter spec): a zero-retention tenant with an OpenRouter key: ZDR option on every attempt, unverified aliases skipped, 409 when none remain, no direct-key fallback; alias-less chain -> no_executable_candidates.

# Test vectors
JSON files for: alias parsing table (shared with the Rust alias bead), workload projection inputs and exact outputs (shared with the projection bead), telemetry item derivation, retention expiry evaluation. Version the vector set.

# Done when
Scenarios and vectors are committed with stable ids and a README describing how an SDK runs them. Commit.

ZR) with stable ids; vectors alias.v1, telemetry.v1, retention.v1 (plus existing projection.p1, normalize.d29); conformance.json manifest with sha256; README on how an SDK runs them; vector replays, scenario schema, and manifest tests

title: Full-stack e2e test script: migrate, seam, corpus, batch chain, recommend, proxy, MCP, privacy checks, with step logs
description:
# What
A full-stack end-to-end test script that exercises the real binaries together, with detailed step logging, and runs in CI with no real providers. It proves the pieces that each package tested alone actually work as one system.

# Script (`scripts/e2e.sh` or an `xtask e2e`, plus a cargo integration test that wraps it)
1. Start Postgres 16 (testcontainers or a docker run), print its URL.
2. `maverick migrate`; assert exit 0.
3. Start the fake-provider HTTP server (scripted responses for the mini-corpus prompts, judge, and classifier) and point every provider base URL at it through engine config.
4. `maverick serve --worker-only` and `maverick serve --api-only` as separate processes (the real deploy shape); wait for `/up`.
5. Through the internal seam: create columns (two providers, one secondary endpoint), create a tenant, issue an API key, set pools/weights/constraints, set a zero-retention tenant with a ZR column.
6. `maverick corpus load` + `activate` with `parity/fixtures/api/testdata/e2e_corpus/`.
7. Enqueue `prediction_lock` and `nightly_smoke` for a fixed night (via an operator trigger or the job client); wait for `aggregate_rebuild`, `regression_scan`, `calibration_score` to finish; assert `batches` rows are completed exactly once.
8. `POST /v1/recommend` (declared and prompt forms); assert pick, chain, flags, trace row, `measured` as expected for one night.
9. Start `maverick-proxy` in self-hosted and hosted modes against the engine and the fake providers; send one chat and one messages request each; assert relay, correlation headers, telemetry arrives in `outcomes`.
10. Privacy spot checks: zero-retention tenant prompt form without a ZR classifier -> 422; canary string in a request appears in no process log.
11. MCP: `tools/list` and one `recommend_model` over `/mcp`.
12. Shut everything down with SIGTERM; assert clean exits and drained alerts.

# Logging
Every step prints a numbered header, the command or request, status, elapsed time, and on failure the last 200 lines of each process log (engine logs are JSON; pretty-print them). Artifacts (process logs, captured requests) go to `target/e2e/<timestamp>/` for CI upload.

# Rules
No real provider, no network beyond localhost, no corpus content (synthetic mini-corpus only). Deterministic: fixed night, fixed clock where the engine allows it.

# Done when
The script passes locally and in CI, and a deliberately broken step produces a readable failure report. Commit.

title: Kamal: the web role's fixed 127.0.0.1:8081 publish breaks every deploy after the first (migrate hook and rolling boot)
description:
# The bug
`config/deploy.yml` (bead 9.4) gives the web role `options: publish: "127.0.0.1:8081:8081"` so operators reach the internal listener over an SSH tunnel to the host loopback. In Kamal 2.12:
- `Kamal::Cli::App::Boot#run` starts the new container, deploys it to kamal-proxy, and only then stops the old one. Both web containers run at once, and the new one cannot bind host port 8081 ("port is already allocated").
- `kamal app exec` without `--reuse` (`execute_in_new_container`) copies `role.option_args`, so the one-off container of the `.kamal/hooks/pre-app-boot` migration and of the `kamal migrate` alias also publishes 8081. It fails while the old web container runs.
`kamal setup` works (nothing runs yet); every later `kamal deploy` fails at the migrate hook. Found while writing the go-live runbook (9.12). The Go-era file (config/deploy-go-reference.yml, reference §9.4) had the same line.

# The fix
Publish nothing from app roles. `scripts/internal-tunnel.sh <user@host>` looks up the running web container's address on the `kamal` network (labels service=maverick, role=web) and opens `ssh -N -L 127.0.0.1:8081:<ip>:8081`. The internal listener stays unrouted and unpublished. Update the deploy.yml comments, docker/README.md, and docs/operations.md.

# Done when
No app role publishes a port, the tunnel script passes shellcheck and resolves the address with the real Kamal labels, and the docs name the script.
close_reason: Completed: no Kamal app role publishes a port; scripts/internal-tunnel.sh tunnels to the web container's kamal-network address; docs updated

title: Spend preview: a read-only 'maverick spend preview' so the owner can size the caps before the cold-start nights (default caps refuse night 1)
description:
# Why (a go-live blocker for 9.6)
At go-live every catalog column is cold_start, and nightly_smoke runs the FULL corpus for cold_start columns (batch.rs groups), 3 repeats, for 5 nights. From the real corpus (aggregates only: 221 tasks, sum est_in 387,959, sum max_tokens 163,100), one cold-start column projects about 1.164 x input_per_mtok + 0.489 x output_per_mtok USD per night: $10.83 for a $3/$15 model, $54 for $15/$75. A 10 to 12 column launch catalog will very likely project over the $100 nightly default on night 1, and the trailing 7-day spend reaches the $500 weekly default by night 4 or 5 (nightly spend counts toward the weekly cap). The batch then refuses (spend_refusal) and bead 9.6's first live nightly does not run. Today the owner can only learn the projection from that refusal.

# What
A hidden, read-only CLI report, `maverick spend preview [--job nightly_smoke|weekly_sweep] [--night YYYY-MM-DD]`, that runs the SAME code as the batch: the same composition (active corpus, runnable columns, the smoke vs cold_start groups), the same projection (project_spend), and the same guard verdict (SpendCheck::decision over the night and week actuals), with the configured repeats and caps. It writes nothing: no batch lease, no alert, no run.
- maverick-jobs: move the batch composition into a shared function used by run_batch and the preview (no behavior change), and split the guard's window read from its alert write.
- Output: per-group and per-column projection, planned runs, night and week spent, both caps, and the verdict (allow, warn, or refuse).
- Hidden like demo-run, so Go's exact MAIN_USAGE text is unchanged.

# Tests
Real Postgres: a seeded corpus (smoke and full tasks), cold_start, active, and retired columns, and runs inside and outside the windows; the preview's numbers are computed by hand, and no alert, lease, or run row is written. The existing batch tests stay green.

# Docs
Runbook section 1 and section 6: run the preview after the corpus load and size both caps for the cold-start week. operations.md "Spend caps".

# Done when
The preview matches the batch's projection and verdict, the tests pass, and the docs name it.

title: Cross-cutting privacy acceptance suite (canary no-log test, zero-retention end to end)
description:
# What
The cross-cutting privacy acceptance suite (spec §15 "Privacy tests", §14.3, §9.10; master plan §6; D1, D2, D13, D15, D17, D19, D30, D39; G5, G13, G14 privacy rule). Each test runs against real Postgres and the fake provider, with numbered step logs and captured process logs printed on failure (bead 1.7).

# Tests
1. Canary (D19): send a prompt-form recommend (engine), a proxy chat request, a proxy messages request, and an MCP `recommend_model` call, each carrying a unique canary string in the prompt, the body, and every credential header. Capture every exported span, every log line (stdout and stderr, all levels including DEBUG), and every metric label (in-memory OTel exporter plus captured logs). Assert the canary appears NOWHERE.
2. A declared request cannot select a `standard` or `unknown` column for a zero-retention tenant.
3. Neither classification nor recommendation sends a zero-retention tenant's prompt or pick to an unverified endpoint (the fake provider records every call).
4. Retention expiry yields `409 no_compliant_columns`, never stale compliance (column and execution-alias expiry both).
5. Zero-retention tenant without a ZR classifier column: prompt form -> `422 zero_retention_requires_declared`, zero classifier calls, nothing stored (no cache row, no capture).
6. Debug capture is refused for zero-retention tenants at window creation (`409 zero_retention_conflict`) and at request time.
7. Hosted proxy with only an OpenAI key never calls Anthropic, and no provider env key is read (D12).
8. Neither the engine key nor the tenant's `X-Maverick-API-Key` appears in any upstream header (D30).
9. No prompt is stored anywhere outside `debug_captures.ciphertext` (scan every text and jsonb column of every table after a prompt-form run for the canary).
10. Zero-retention tenant through the proxy in OpenRouter mode: every attempt carries `provider.zdr: true`, unverified aliases are skipped, all-unverified -> 409, never a direct-key fallback (D15).
11. Tenant telemetry opt-out (D39): with `telemetry_opt_out` set, recommend returns `telemetry: false`, the proxy sends zero telemetry bytes for that tenant, a hand-sent telemetry batch writes zero `outcomes` rows, and another tenant's telemetry is unaffected.
12. Global telemetry off (`MAVERICK_PROXY_TELEMETRY=off`): zero bytes to `/v1/telemetry` (G13).

# Done when
All tests pass in CI. Commit.
close_reason: Privacy acceptance suite (44fe410): crates/acceptance, canary (D19) plus 11 privacy tests on the real engine and proxy; no leak found

title: Build the hot-path latency harness (declared p95 < 50 ms, uncached prompt p95 < 1.8 s, proxy TTFB)

A `maverick` subcommand or `xtask` that reads the Go-era aggregates and the first Rust nightly's aggregates from the same database and reports:

title: G5: a failed alert webhook delivery logs the full webhook URL (its secret) in the error field
description:
# The leak (found in a G5 audit, 2026-09-30)
crates/maverick-alerts/src/webhook.rs Webhook::deliver maps a failed POST to `err.to_string()`. reqwest 0.13.5's Error Display ends with ` for url (<url>)`, the full URL: its path, its query, and any user:password. fanout.rs deliver_with_retries logs that text as `error` on every failed attempt (warn "alert delivery attempt failed"), and again when it gives up (error "alert delivery failed").

Webhook URLs often carry their secret in the path or the query. The config crate says so and shows only the origin in Config's Debug (maverick-config origin_only, G5). So when the receiver is unreachable (DNS, connect, TLS, timeout), up to 5 log lines per alert carry the credential. G5 and §14.3: credentials never appear in log fields. D19 already covers this, so no new divergence is needed. The reference pins only the fields {destination, alert_id, attempt, error}, not the text.

# Fix
- webhook.rs: drop the URL from the transport error (`reqwest::Error::without_url`). Keep the cause chain (connect refused, DNS, TLS), which carries no URL, so the operator still sees why it failed.
- Test (maverick-alerts): a webhook URL with a canary token in its path and query, pointing at a closed port. Deliver through the fan-out with init_test_tracing_with_secrets. The canary appears in no log line, and the lines still name the webhook destination and the failure.

# Also checked, clean
maverick-proxy and maverick-core log sites, the engine-client errors, the maverick-config issue texts and Debug, the SMTP errors (url::ParseError and SMTP replies carry no URL), and the mcp-stdio auth error. The Google key travels in x-goog-api-key, not the URL.
close_reason: Webhook transport errors drop the URL (keep the cause chain); Webhook Debug shows the origin only; tests/webhook_redaction.rs proves both (fails on the old code). maverick-alerts suites, clippy, fmt, instrument lint green.

title: Document the zero_retention_evidence classifier_degraded alerts in spec §8.3, operations.md, and observability.md (ke10 follow-up)
description:
model-maverick-ke10 added two classifier_degraded alerts for the column that classifier.zero_retention_column names. The spec and the operator docs do not describe them yet.

# What the code does (crates/maverick-api/src/classifier_evidence.rs)
- The column resolves (find_column, the a49j rule), but its effective retention is not zero: one critical classifier_degraded, subject {classifier_column, column_id, reason: "zero_retention_evidence", zero_retention_column}.
- The evidence is valid again: one info classifier_degraded with reason "zero_retention_evidence_restored".
- It runs after PUT /internal/v1/columns/{id}, at boot, and on each D41 refresh (every 5 min), so expiry with no write is caught too. The newest matching alert row is the state, so the callers never alert twice for one change.
- An unset ref writes nothing, and so does a ref that matches no column. D41's unresolved alert covers the second case.

# Work
1. Spec §8.3, the zero-retention bullet: one sentence for the two alerts and the subject, next to the D41 text. Mark it "(changed for the Rust port)", as the other §8.3 changes are.
2. docs/operations.md: what an operator does on the critical alert (restore the column's evidence, or re-point classifier.zero_retention_column).
3. docs/architecture/observability.md: add the two reasons to the classifier_degraded alert list.

# Done when
All three files describe both reasons and the subject, and the wording follows the AGENTS.md writing rules.
close_reason: Spec 8.3, docs/operations.md (Kinds row and operator steps), and docs/architecture/observability.md describe both zero_retention_evidence reasons and the subject, as classifier_evidence.rs has them. Docs only; the boundary tier passes.

title: OWNER: an SDK core that has not seen a response yet cannot know a tenant is zero-retention, so a cold-process MM outage fails open (G14)
description:
# Question for the owner (found in the zero-retention audit, 2026-09-30)
G14: "for a zero-retention tenant, fallback may use only cached chain entries stamped retention_mode: zero, and the static default or original model only if locally configured as verified zero-retention; otherwise the call fails closed."

What the SDK contract and maverick-core do (sdk-v0 plan §2.1, crates/maverick-core/src/failopen.rs):
- The core learns that a tenant is zero-retention only from MM: a response with zero_retention: true, or a terminal privacy error. It keeps that in memory, and the plan forbids disk state.
- Conformance S06h and S06i (plan scenario 6(c)) cover a "cold" outage only after a zero_retention: true response has been seen.
- In a freshly started process whose first call finds MM down, the tenant is unknown and the ladder treats it as ordinary. It falls open to MODELMAVERICK_DEFAULT_MODEL, or to the caller's original model, even when that model is not in MODELMAVERICK_ZERO_RETENTION_VERIFIED. So the zero-retention customer's prompt goes to an unverified model. The customer's own credentials are used, but G14's "fails closed" does not hold.

The proxy is not affected today: it never fails open (502 engine_error).

# Options
(a) A local declaration: MODELMAVERICK_ZERO_RETENTION=true (config zero_retention: true). The core starts the tenant as zero-retention: the declared form from the first call, and the zero-retention ladder in an outage. A later zero_retention: false response does not clear a local true. This needs sdk-v0 plan §2.1 and §2.3 changes, a conformance scenario (a cold process plus an outage, failing closed), and the four external SDKs.
(b) Tie it to the existing setting: when MODELMAVERICK_ZERO_RETENTION_VERIFIED is non-empty, treat an unknown tenant as zero-retention until MM answers. There is no new variable, but the rule is implicit.
(c) Accept and document: a zero-retention customer sets MODELMAVERICK_PRIVACY=declared and configures only verified models as the default. The docs say that the protection starts after the first MM answer.

Recommendation: (a). It is explicit, it also covers the privacy mode, and it costs one variable. The engine is unchanged.

title: Self-hosted engine: offline license, origin and replica roles, safe upgrades (D48 to D50)
description:
# Goal

Let customers (financial and health-data companies) run the engine inside their own networks, including sealed ones, with the same build that runs Maverick's hosted deployment, and upgrade it without breaking installs. Proposed divergences D48 (license), D49 (roles and matrix bundles), D50 (compatibility). Full design: `plans/self-hosted-engine-plan.md`. Read it first.

# Shape

- One signed release, two roles: `origin` (hosted, holds the corpus, benchmarks, publishes bundles) and `replica` (customer, no corpus, imports signed matrix bundles). The corpus never leaves Maverick.
- Offline Ed25519 license file (`mmlic1`), public keys compiled in, no network call. States valid, grace, lapsed; `updates_until` gates new releases and bundles. No plans, prices, or tiers: billing stays in the control plane.
- Lapsed stops recommend with 503 only; SDK and proxy fail-open keep customer calls working; audit stays readable.
- A replica is single-tenant: one customer organization, bootstrapped with one tenant and one API key on first start; no tenant management.
- Sealed by default: no outbound call unless configured.
- Upgrade rules: SemVer, additive /v1, feature header so new clients never send fields an old engine rejects, additive migrations with a 12-month upgrade window, one upgrade command `maverick upgrade` (preflight, plan, apply, record, verify; `--check` for change control), serve never migrates, upgrade and skew matrices in CI.

# Done when

Every child bead is closed, the spec and DIVERGENCES.md carry D48 to D50, and the sealed-environment, upgrade-matrix, and skew-matrix tests pass in CI.

title: OWNER: answer the self-hosted engine open questions (plan §11)
description:
OWNER: answer `plans/self-hosted-engine-plan.md` §11. Each has a recommendation; the beads assume it unless the answer differs.

1. Lapsed license: `503 license_lapsed` on recommend only (recommended), or never stop recommend and gate only releases and bundles.
2. Lengths: 30 days grace, 12-month upgrade window, 12-month skew window, 30-night bundle window (recommended).
3. Replicas never run corpus benchmarks; customer tasks stay v2 (recommended).
4. `MAVERICK_MATRIX_PULL_URL` for connected installs, off by default (recommended).
5. A separate signing tool binary; private keys never in the repository (recommended).

Done when: answers are recorded here and in plan §11 (edit the plan where an answer differs), then close.

title: Matrix bundle import on replicas, local price overrides, optional pull (D49)
description:
Matrix bundle import on replicas (D49, `plans/self-hosted-engine-plan.md` §5.2, §5.3).

Work:
1. `maverick matrix import <path>`: verify signature, hashes, format version, schema range, and `published_at <= updates_until` from the license. One transaction: upsert catalog (keep local latency data and local pricing overrides), append aggregates marked with the bundle's matrix_version, switch the active matrix_version. Same bundle twice: no-op. Older than active: refuse unless `--allow-older`.
2. `maverick matrix status`: active matrix_version, published_at, import time, days behind.
3. Local price override: the internal column PUT can set a local pricing snapshot flagged as local; imports never overwrite it.
4. Optional pull: `MAVERICK_MATRIX_PULL_URL` hourly with the same verification; off by default.
5. A replica with no bundle serves cold start (G1).
6. Alert `matrix_stale` (warning) when the active matrix is older than 7 days.

Tests (real Postgres): each refusal; transaction rollback on failure; local overrides survive; no-op re-import; recommend ranks from imported aggregates exactly as the origin does for the same data (golden). Done when: committed and pushed.

title: Single-tenant replicas: bootstrap one tenant and key, maverick key CLI, refuse tenant admin (D49)
description:
Single-tenant replicas: bootstrap, key CLI, and refusals (D49, `plans/self-hosted-engine-plan.md` §6).

Owner direction 2026-09-30: a self-hosted customer is one organization. They buy a license, download the release, install it, and set the license key. They never create or manage tenants. The engine keeps its multi-tenant model for the hosted origin.

Work (replica role only; origin unchanged):
1. Bootstrap: on the first `serve` start with no tenant, create exactly one tenant named from the license `licensee`, with the default pool and default constraints (same code as `POST /internal/v1/tenants`), and one API key. Print the key once; also write it to `MAVERICK_BOOTSTRAP_KEY_FILE` (mode 0600) when set. Idempotent: never runs again once a tenant exists. Safe under concurrent starts (advisory lock).
2. `maverick key create | list | revoke`: manage the one tenant's keys, same code and audit records as the internal API; actor `cli:<os user>`; the tenant is implicit.
3. On a replica, `POST /internal/v1/tenants`, tenant suspend and activate, and `PUT /internal/v1/tenants/{id}/limits` return `409 single_tenant_install` (message in the spec). Health detail and column administration still work.
4. Pools, constraints, weights, and zero retention are configured through the normal tenant API with a key; nothing new.

Tests (real Postgres): first start creates one tenant and one key; second start creates nothing; concurrent first starts create one; key file mode 0600; key commands round trip and write audit rows; each refused endpoint returns 409 on a replica and works on an origin. Done when: committed and pushed.

Work:
1. Sealed test: start a replica with default outbound settings in a network namespace with no route out (or a container with `--network none` plus a local Postgres), let it bootstrap its tenant and key, import a fixture bundle, run a declared recommend with the bootstrapped key, assert success and zero outbound connection attempts.
2. Release pipeline: container image and static binary tarball, cosign signature for the image, detached signature for the tarball, CycloneDX SBOM, `cargo deny` report, and an offline install kit (image tarball, checksums, migration list).
3. Skew matrix in CI: current SDK core and proxy against the previous engine release; previous proxy against the current engine.

Writing rules from AGENTS.md apply; do not use the word matched by `tr[i]al`. Done when: documents agree, committed and pushed.

title: Version surface: maverick --version and engine version and feature headers (D50)
description:
Version surface (D50, `plans/self-hosted-engine-plan.md` §7.1). Everything else reports through it, so it goes first.

Work:
1. `maverick --version`: semver (from Cargo), release date (set at build time from an env var in the release pipeline; dev builds print `dev` and today's date), git commit, minimum schema version, accepted license and bundle format versions. Add it to the usage text.
2. Every public and internal response carries `X-Maverick-Engine-Version` and `X-Maverick-API-Features` (a tower layer). The feature list is a const in one place; start it with the features that exist when this lands.
3. The proxy stamps its own `X-Maverick-Proxy-Version`.

Tests: header present on every route including errors and `/up`; `--version` output shape; the feature list is sorted and has no duplicates. Done when: committed and pushed.

title: Offline license verification, states, 503 when lapsed, health and alerts (D48)
description:
License verification and states in the engine (D48, `plans/self-hosted-engine-plan.md` §4).

Work:
1. Parser and verifier for `mmlic1.<payload>.<sig>`: Ed25519 (RustCrypto `ed25519-dalek`; add to `cargo deny` allow list) over the exact bytes `mmlic1.` + payload text; embedded public keys by `kid`; required fields; unknown fields ignored; 24 h `not_before` tolerance. Pure code in a domain crate, no I/O.
2. Loading from `MAVERICK_LICENSE_FILE` or `MAVERICK_LICENSE` (exactly one); reload every 10 min and on SIGHUP; a bad new license is logged and ignored. Never log the raw text.
3. Startup refusals with named reasons (missing, bad signature, unknown kid, wrong role, unknown format, future not_before, release date after `updates_until`).
4. States valid, grace, lapsed from the clock. Lapsed: `POST /v1/recommend` and MCP `recommend_model` return `503 license_lapsed`; all else works; `/up` unaffected.
5. `license` component in `GET /health/detail`; alerts `license_expiring` (60/30/7 days) and `license_expired` (daily in grace and lapsed) through the existing alerts path, deduped.
6. `maverick license show` prints the fields.
7. Test keys: a fixed test key pair under test data only; the test public key is compiled in only under `cfg(test)` or a test feature, never in release builds (add a test that a release build rejects a test-signed license).

Tests: vectors for every refusal; state boundaries (exact instants); reload; 503 contract test; health and alert tests; no raw license in logs (canary). `cargo-mutants` on the verifier and state code. Done when: committed and pushed.

title: maverick-license signing tool and key custody docs (D48)
description:
License signing tool (D48, `plans/self-hosted-engine-plan.md` §11 question 5).

Work:
1. New binary crate `crates/maverick-license`: `issue` (fields as flags, private key from a file path or an env var at run time, prints the license), `verify` (with a public key file), `keygen` (writes a key pair to files the operator chooses). It shares the format code with the engine verifier.
2. Private keys never enter the repository; add `*.key` style ignore rules and a CI check that no Ed25519 private key PEM or raw seed is tracked.
3. `docs/operations.md`: key custody, rotation (new kid, ship the public key in a release, then issue with it), and emergency revocation (there is no online revocation; a short-expiry reissue is the tool).

Tests: issue then verify round trip; engine accepts a tool-issued license signed with a test key; tampered payload rejected. Done when: committed and pushed.

title: maverick upgrade command, upgrade rules, and the upgrade matrix in CI (D50)
description:
`maverick upgrade`, database upgrade rules, and the upgrade matrix (D50, `plans/self-hosted-engine-plan.md` §7.3, §7.4, §7.7). Owner decision 2026-09-30: upgrading is one command, `maverick upgrade`.

Work:
1. `serve` never migrates: it refuses to start while engine or graphile_worker migrations are pending, with the message `run maverick upgrade`.
2. Shared safety checks (used by both `upgrade` and `migrate`): newer database (applied migrations this binary does not know; map sqlx's error to a message naming both versions); the 12-month upgrade window (record each release's highest migration in a checked-in table so the check is data, not dates; the message names the intermediate release).
3. `maverick upgrade` per plan §7.4: preflight (state printout, newer-DB, window, license allows this release and role, active bundle format readable, Postgres advisory upgrade lock, running `serve` processes vs online-safe migrations using a heartbeat row with each process's release), plan (migrations with `online-safe` or `needs-downtime`), apply (same code as `migrate`, inside the lock), record (new `upgrades` table: from, to, started, finished, operator, migrations), verify. Flags `--check` (preflight and plan only, no changes), `--yes`, `--json`. Without `--yes`: prompt in a terminal, refuse when not a terminal. Add it to the usage text.
4. `serve` writes the heartbeat row (release, host label, last seen) every 30 s; rows older than 2 minutes count as stopped.
5. Migration header comment `-- class: online-safe` or `-- class: needs-downtime`; a CI check refuses a migration without one. Mark every existing migration (all are additive, so online-safe; confirm each).
6. `maverick migrate` stays (Go parity, dev, CI) with the shared checks only; its usage text points operators to `maverick upgrade`.
7. Upgrade matrix CI: a fixed populated scenario (tenants, keys, pools, constraints, traces, aggregates); a dump per release kept under test data; each run upgrades each dump with `maverick upgrade --yes` and runs the contract and history tests on it. Seed the first dump from the current release.
8. Document expand and contract and the migration classes in `docs/operations.md` and `crates/maverick-store/migrations/README.md`.

title: Hide columns without valid zero-retention evidence from /v1/policies for zero-retention tenants
description:

title: Retry classifier column and judge pool resolution after startup instead of resolving only at boot
description:
Owner decision (2026-09-29): the engine must not stay degraded until a restart when the classifier column or judge pool cannot be resolved at startup. This is a new intended difference from Go.

Today (Go parity, engine-reference startup steps 9 and 10): the API resolves MAVERICK_CLASSIFIER_COLUMN (and MAVERICK_CLASSIFIER_ZERO_RETENTION_COLUMN) against the catalog once at boot. On failure it logs ERROR 'classifier column unavailable; prompt-path requests will receive the fallback classification' and serves fallback_default classifications (and 422 zero_retention_requires_declared for zero-retention tenants) until restart. The worker resolves MAVERICK_JUDGE_POOL once too; on failure judge_rubric gradings fail until restart. With a fresh database the API can easily boot before the catalog has these columns.

Work:
1. Add a DIVERGENCES.md row and update the spec (§8.3 classifier, judge pool section, startup/operations) with the new rule.
2. When resolution fails at boot, retry in the background with backoff (for example every 30 to 60 seconds) until it succeeds; when it succeeds, log INFO and start using the classifier or judge pool without a restart. Keep serving with the current fallback until then (G1 unchanged; zero-retention still fails closed).
3. Make the degraded state visible: raise an alert (reuse classifier_degraded or add a kind; spec it) while the classifier is unresolved for more than a few minutes, since no classifier calls means the failure-rate alert never fires.
4. Consider also re-resolving when the catalog changes (column added, retired, or retention evidence expiring) so a stale resolution does not stick; at minimum document the behavior.
5. Tests: boot with the column missing, insert it, and assert prompt-path requests switch from fallback_default to the real classifier without restart; same for the judge pool; alert raised and cleared.

Done when: spec and DIVERGENCES updated, tests pass, committed and pushed to main.
